3:110.ar: كُنتُمۡ خَيۡرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخۡرِجَتۡ لِلنَّاسِ تَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ ءَامَنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۚ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَأَكۡثَرُهُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
3:110.en: Ye are the best community that hath been raised up for mankind. Ye enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency; and ye believe in Allah. And if the People of the Scripture had believed it had been better for them. Some of them are believers; but most of them are evil-livers

3:104.ar: وَلۡتَكُن مِّنكُمۡ أُمَّةࣱ يَدۡعُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡخَيۡرِ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
3:104.en: And there may spring from you a nation who invite to goodness, and enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency. Such are they who are successful

9:67.ar: ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ بَعۡضُهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡضࣲۚ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَقۡبِضُونَ أَيۡدِيَهُمۡۚ نَسُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَنَسِيَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
9:67.en: The hypocrites, both men and women, proceed one from another. They enjoin the wrong, and they forbid the right, and they withhold their hands (from spending for the cause of Allah). They forget Allah, so He hath forgotten them. Lo! the hypocrites, they are the transgressors

7:157.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ ٱلۡأُمِّيَّ ٱلَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكۡتُوبًا عِندَهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ يَأۡمُرُهُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَىٰهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡخَبَٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنۡهُمۡ إِصۡرَهُمۡ وَٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ ٱلَّتِي كَانَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
7:157.en: Those who follow the messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write, whom they will find described in the Torah and the Gospel (which are) with them. He will enjoin on them that which is right and forbid them that which is wrong. He will make lawful for them all good things and prohibit for them only the foul; and he will relieve them of their burden and the fetters that they used to wear. Then those who believe in him, and honour him, and help him, and follow the light which is sent down with him: they are the successful

5:78.ar: لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُۥدَ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
5:78.en: Those of the Children of Israel who went astray were cursed by the tongue of David, and of Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they rebelled and used to transgress

5:79.ar: كَانُواْ لَا يَتَنَاهَوۡنَ عَن مُّنكَرࣲ فَعَلُوهُۚ لَبِئۡسَ مَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
5:79.en: They restrained not one another from the wickedness they did. Verily evil was that they used to do

1dyEQb_G4Ic.speaker: adnan
1dyEQb_G4Ic.speaker_note: Continues his own Aqabah series ('I have shared with you the first two articles') and speaks of having lived most of his life in the Middle East.
1dyEQb_G4Ic.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Third Article, Reforming Social Values
1dyEQb_G4Ic.one_line: The third article of the pledge: commanding good and forbidding wrong as social reform, distinct from dawah, and why Muslims must stop staying silent.
1dyEQb_G4Ic.summary: The fifth khutbah in his Pledge of Al-Aqabah series takes the third article: the Ansar's commitment to reform social values by commanding the good and forbidding the wrong. If the Ansar had to offer these articles for the Prophet to enter their lives, fairness says we must offer the same. He argues that ma'ruf and munkar are social terms, what a society recognizes as good or bad. Aal-Imran 3:110 grounds the ummah's excellence in this work, and the Quran defines both the hypocrites and the Prophet by it. Missed prayers and personal rituals belong to dawah, which has its own art; munkar is behaviour that damages society, and there privacy ends. His examples are line-jumping, which he never saw respected in the Middle East, a youth smoking, drug use and casual cohabitation. Because Muslims did not speak up early, they are now on the defensive, unable to call the filthy filthy. Every prophet was a reformer, and the Prophet refused Quraysh's offer to accept Islam if they need not sit with slaves. In the second khutbah he mocks Muslims who found law and order here and failed to champion it, and asks people to carry their values with pride, with knowledge, wisdom and good manners.

outline.heading: Opening
Why we must offer the same pledge
outline.gist: The Ansar offered the pledge and the Prophet entered their lives and made them central to his story. Fairness says that if we hope for the same place in his legacy, and to be among those he calls "my nation" on the Day of Judgment, we must offer the same articles.

outline.heading: The third article: reforming social values
outline.gist: After adherence in ease and hardship and committing wealth, the third article is a commitment to reform social values. He must first explain how this Quranic term differs from what overlaps with it.

outline.heading: The best nation, because of this work
outline.gist: In Aal-Imran 3:110 Allah calls this the best nation ever brought out for humanity and explains it by commanding good and forbidding wrong, naming belief in Allah third, after these two.

outline.heading: Ma'ruf and munkar have a social definition
outline.gist: The Ansar understood the terms at once; we do not. In the same surah, 3:104 asks for a group who call to good and command it. Ma'ruf and munkar are defined socially: a people's norms carry weight, so you learn what a society holds good and bad, reinforce what you agree with and work to reform what you do not.

outline.heading: Not praying is a sin; munkar is social
outline.gist: Not praying is wrong, but strictly it is a personal sin, while munkar is behaviour society has a view on and that affects society at large. Neglected rituals are addressed through dawah, which has its own art and will come later in the series.

outline.heading: The hypocrites, defined by the reverse
outline.gist: At-Tawbah 9:67 defines the hypocrites as those who command wrong, forbid good and close their hands: they go against two of the pledge's five articles.

outline.heading: The Prophet described to earlier faiths
outline.gist: In Al-A'raf 7:157, when the Quran tells earlier faiths who the Prophet would be, it starts with social values: he commands good, forbids wrong and reforms what goes against the word of Allah.

outline.heading: Every prophet a reformer, and it costs popularity
outline.gist: Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb and Musa each had a unique reform challenge. This is an article of the pledge because it is unpopular: the moment you say "that is not okay", your popularity goes.

outline.heading: Whoever sees a wrong: the line-cutter
outline.gist: The hadith says "whoever sees": you have no authority to change a private sin by hand. But here people respect lines, while in the Middle East, where he lived most of his life, he never once stood in one and shoving and nepotism are the norm. When someone cuts in, you intervene, because values dissolve once no one defends them; Muslims a thousand years ago stood in line too.

outline.heading: Privacy ends where social values are damaged
outline.gist: A minor smoking in public should be told it is not okay, even though anyone who gets involved in other people's business is now called names. You have your privacy, but it ends when your behaviour attacks good social values; if you do not pray, that is between you and dawah.

outline.heading: When munkar becomes ma'ruf, nothing is left
outline.gist: When wrong becomes accepted and good becomes condemned, no room is left for Islam to be practised. That is why the Prophet asked for this article: he came to challenge the status quo, not to bless it.

outline.heading: Drugs, cohabitation and our silence
outline.gist: Drug and alcohol use is socially accepted here but frowned on officially, a value Muslims share and should push further. Couples living together for years is not seen as a problem, yet it shapes how people build relationships and families, and because Muslims did not speak up they are now on the defensive against a tsunami of change.

outline.heading: The reforms the Ansar accepted
outline.gist: We are now scared for our own definitions because we did not speak early. The Ansar understood what the article meant: slavery frowned upon and slaves freed, domestic abuse ended, women choosing their spouses, inheriting, working and owning their wealth, none of which was so in pre-Islamic Arabia.

outline.heading: Quraysh's offer: just don't sit us with the slaves
outline.gist: Like today, tribes asked him not to touch their wealth or how they treated youth, slaves and women. The leaders of Makkah offered to accept Islam on one condition: that they not sit with the slaves.

outline.heading: Equality is not negotiable
outline.gist: He refused outright, because human equality regardless of origin, colour, lineage or wealth is a value. Winning over the leaders of Makkah did not matter: you accept Islam as it is and do not get to change it.

outline.heading: Bani Isra'il cursed for letting it go
outline.gist: Al-Ma'idah 5:78-79: the disbelievers of Bani Isra'il were cursed on the tongues of Dawud and Isa because they saw wrong and let it pass, because the person was known, wealthy or popular, or out of fear of being unpopular. Enjoy a society with no shared idea of right and wrong.

outline.heading: Silence, and speaking without knowledge
outline.gist: Without reinforcing good and stopping bad, society becomes a chaotic melting pot of garbage. Those who do speak often lack the knowledge and make it worse; this must be done collectively and communally, or we lose our identity.

outline.heading: No one knows it better than a Muslim Canadian
outline.gist: A Muslim Canadian feels this without needing any education: you can no longer use certain adjectives, normalize what is normal or call something filthy unacceptable. The Ansar knew the article was hard and offered it anyway.

outline.heading: Interlude
Champion the good values you find
outline.gist: A Muslim community entering a society analyzes its good and bad social values, then reinforces and champions the good ones; we came and found an organized society.

outline.heading: Champions of lining up?
outline.gist: With sarcasm he asks whether Muslims who left years of chaos and found law and order here became its champions, standing in line, driving well and following the law. Finding a good value and not championing it, or working against it, means you did not understand your deen.

outline.heading: And chastity?
outline.gist: He continues the sarcasm about the bad values found here, such as the lack of chastity: did Muslim young men stay out of it? How can things work out if an article the Ansar pledged is not even considered an issue?

outline.heading: Values held with pride, not convenience
outline.gist: Carry your values with pride and protect them with your lives; push forward with those who share them and push back on those who do not. A value is not a matter of convenience or compromise, and all the prophets were exiled or killed for challenging the status quo.

outline.heading: Knowledge, wisdom and his politeness
outline.gist: Shu'ayb and Lut said "we will not behave like this". It takes knowledge, wisdom and finesse, not yelling at each other outside, and the Prophet's etiquette and gentle speech are themselves a value we have lost.

outline.heading: Interlude
Not about dress or tattoos at the masjid
outline.gist: Do not restrict this article to someone who comes to the masjid with a tattoo or improperly dressed; that is a personal matter for dawah. This is about defending good social values and removing bad ones, before a tsunami of bad values overtakes us all.

outline.heading: Outro

45:2.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
45:2.en: The revelation of the Scripture is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

45:3.ar: إِنَّ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
45:3.en: Lo! in the heavens and the earth are portents for believers

45:4.ar: وَفِي خَلۡقِكُمۡ وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَآبَّةٍ ءَايَٰتࣱ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُوقِنُونَ
45:4.en: And in your creation, and all the beasts that He scattereth in the earth, are portents for a folk whose faith is sure

45:5.ar: وَٱخۡتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن رِّزۡقࣲ فَأَحۡيَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَا وَتَصۡرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَٰحِ ءَايَٰتࣱ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
45:5.en: And the difference of night and day and the provision that Allah sendeth down from the sky and thereby quickeneth the earth after her death, and the ordering of the winds, are portents for a people who have sense

45:6.ar: تِلۡكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتۡلُوهَا عَلَيۡكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثِۭ بَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ وَءَايَٰتِهِۦ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
45:6.en: These are the portents of Allah which We recite unto thee (Muhammad) with truth. Then in what fact, after Allah and His portents, will they believe

45:8.ar: يَسۡمَعُ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسۡتَكۡبِرࣰ ا كَأَن لَّمۡ يَسۡمَعۡهَاۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
45:8.en: Who heareth the revelations of Allah recited unto him, and then continueth in pride as though he heard them not. Give him tidings of a painful doom

45:9.ar: وَإِذَا عَلِمَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا شَيۡـًٔا ٱتَّخَذَهَا هُزُوًاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
45:9.en: And when he knoweth aught of Our revelations he maketh it a jest. For such there is a shameful doom

45:10.ar: مِّن وَرَآئِهِمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَلَا يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُم مَّا كَسَبُواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا مَا ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡلِيَآءَۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
45:10.en: Beyond them there is hell, and that which they have earned will naught avail them, nor those whom they have chosen for protecting friends beside Allah. Theirs will be an awful doom

45:11.ar: هَٰذَا هُدࣰ ىۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مِّن رِّجۡزٍ أَلِيمٌ
45:11.en: This is guidance. And those who disbelieve the revelations of their Lord, for them there is a painful doom of wrath

45:12.ar: ۞ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ لِتَجۡرِيَ ٱلۡفُلۡكُ فِيهِ بِأَمۡرِهِۦ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
45:12.en: Allah it is Who hath made the sea of service unto you that the ships may run thereon by His command, and that ye may seek of His bounty, and that haply ye may be thankful

45:13.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا مِّنۡهُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
45:13.en: And hath made of service unto you whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth; it is all from Him. Lo! herein verily are portents for a people who reflect

45:14.ar: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يَغۡفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرۡجُونَ أَيَّامَ ٱللَّهِ لِيَجۡزِيَ قَوۡمَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
45:14.en: Tell those who believe to forgive those who hope not for the days of Allah; in order that He may requite folk what they used to earn

45:15.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَنۡ أَسَآءَ فَعَلَيۡهَاۖ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمۡ تُرۡجَعُونَ
45:15.en: Whoso doeth right, it is for his soul, and whoso doeth wrong, it is against it. And afterward unto your Lord ye will be brought back

45:16.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحُكۡمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَ وَرَزَقۡنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
45:16.en: And verily we gave the Children of Israel the Scripture and the Command and the Prophethood, and provided them with good things and favoured them above (all) peoples

45:17.ar: وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم بَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُوٓاْ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡعِلۡمُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقۡضِي بَيۡنَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَ
45:17.en: And gave them plain commandments. And they differed not until after the knowledge came unto them, through rivalry among themselves. Lo! thy Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ

45:18.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَٰكَ عَلَىٰ شَرِيعَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ فَٱتَّبِعۡهَا وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
45:18.en: And now have We set thee (O Muhammad) on a clear road of (Our) commandment; so follow it, and follow not the whims of those who know not

45:19.ar: إِنَّهُمۡ لَن يُغۡنُواْ عَنكَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ بَعۡضࣲۖ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
45:19.en: Lo! they can avail thee naught against Allah. And lo! as for the wrong-doers, some of them are friends of others; and Allah is the Friend of those who ward off (evil)

45:20.ar: هَٰذَا بَصَٰٓئِرُ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣱ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُوقِنُونَ
45:20.en: This is clear indication for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy for a folk whose faith is sure

45:21.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱجۡتَرَحُواْ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ أَن نَّجۡعَلَهُمۡ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ سَوَآءࣰ مَّحۡيَاهُمۡ وَمَمَاتُهُمۡۚ سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ
45:21.en: Or do those who commit ill-deeds suppose that We shall make them as those who believe and do good works, the same in life and death? Bad is their judgment

45:22.ar: وَخَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلِتُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
45:22.en: And Allah hath created the heavens and the earth with truth, and that every soul may be repaid what it hath earned. And they will not be wronged

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Hast thou seen him who maketh his desire his god, and Allah sendeth him astray purposely, and sealeth up his hearing and his heart, and setteth on his sight a covering? Then who will lead him after Allah (hath condemned him)? Will ye not then heed

45:24.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَا هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا ٱلدُّنۡيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحۡيَا وَمَا يُهۡلِكُنَآ إِلَّا ٱلدَّهۡرُۚ وَمَا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
45:24.en: And they say: There is naught but our life of the world; we die and we live, and naught destroyeth us save time; when they have no knowledge whatsoever of (all) that; they do but guess

45:25.ar: وَإِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُنَا بَيِّنَٰتࣲ مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُواْ ٱئۡتُواْ بِـَٔابَآئِنَآ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
45:25.en: And when Our clear revelations are recited unto them their only argument is that they say: Bring (back) our fathers. then, if ye are truthful

45:26.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُ يُحۡيِيكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يَجۡمَعُكُمۡ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
45:26.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Allah giveth life to you, then causeth you to die, then gathereth you unto the Day of Resurrection whereof there is no doubt. But most of mankind know not

45:27.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَيَوۡمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَخۡسَرُ ٱلۡمُبۡطِلُونَ
45:27.en: And unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; and on the day when the Hour riseth, on that day those who follow falsehood will be lost

45:28.ar: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةࣲ جَاثِيَةࣰۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةࣲ تُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:28.en: And thou wilt see each nation crouching, each nation summoned to its record. (And it will be said unto them): This day ye are requited what ye used to do

45:29.ar: هَٰذَا كِتَٰبُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيۡكُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسۡتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:29.en: This Our Book pronounceth against you with truth. Lo! We have caused (all) that ye did to be recorded

45:30.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَيُدۡخِلُهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ فِي رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
45:30.en: Then, as for those who believed and did good works, their Lord will bring them in unto His mercy. That is the evident triumph

45:31.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَفَلَمۡ تَكُنۡ ءَايَٰتِي تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَكۡبَرۡتُمۡ وَكُنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا مُّجۡرِمِينَ
45:31.en: And as for those who disbelieved (it will be said unto them): Were not Our revelations recited unto you? But ye were scornful and became a guilty folk

45:32.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهَا قُلۡتُم مَّا نَدۡرِي مَا ٱلسَّاعَةُ إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنࣰّ ا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُسۡتَيۡقِنِينَ
45:32.en: And when it was said: Lo! Allah's promise is the truth, and there is no doubt of the Hour's coming, ye said: We know not what the Hour is. We deem it naught but a conjecture, and we are by no means convinced

45:33.ar: وَبَدَا لَهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا عَمِلُواْ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
45:33.en: And the evils of what they did will appear unto them, and that which they used to deride will befall them

45:34.ar: وَقِيلَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ نَنسَىٰكُمۡ كَمَا نَسِيتُمۡ لِقَآءَ يَوۡمِكُمۡ هَٰذَا وَمَأۡوَىٰكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
45:34.en: And it will be said: This day We forget you, even as ye forgot the meeting of this your day; and your habitation is the Fire, and there is none to help you

45:35.ar: ذَٰلِكُم بِأَنَّكُمُ ٱتَّخَذۡتُمۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ هُزُوࣰ ا وَغَرَّتۡكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا يُخۡرَجُونَ مِنۡهَا وَلَا هُمۡ يُسۡتَعۡتَبُونَ
45:35.en: This, forasmuch as ye made the revelations of Allah a jest, and the life of the world beguiled you. Therefor this day they come not forth from thence, nor can they make amends

45:36.ar: فَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَرَبِّ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
45:36.en: Then praise be to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, the Lord of the Worlds

45:37.ar: وَلَهُ ٱلۡكِبۡرِيَآءُ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
45:37.en: And unto Him (alone) belongeth Majesty in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

2a8wi2_ueUQ.speaker: adnan

2a8wi2_ueUQ.title: Surat Al-Jathiyah Summary
2a8wi2_ueUQ.one_line: Al-Jathiyah warns four groups against arrogance: disbelievers, believers, the knowledgeable and whole nations, and ends with praise as its cure.
2a8wi2_ueUQ.summary: Al-Jathiyah is the sixth surah of the Ha-Mim cluster and its third warning: vanity and arrogance are a lethal disease. It opens with signs in the cosmos, each verse ending on a higher state, from faith to certainty to understanding, building up to the warnings. First the disbeliever who lies knowingly, hears the signs and turns away in arrogance and mockery. Then the believers: everything was made subservient to them, and they are told to forgive those who do not hope for Allah's days. Using the deen as a means of arrogance toward non-Muslims is, he says, worse than the disbeliever's arrogance, because you know the truth. The Prophet is told to hold firmly to the shari'ah; cherry-picking the deen creates cracks through which arrogance seeps in. Third, people of knowledge of any kind can take their desires as their god and be led astray despite knowing, as seen in how many educated people today have lost faith. Finally, on the Day of Judgment whole nations kneel, each called to its book, held accountable as societies for abandoning the weak and poor. Everyone will be humble eventually; the choice is now or then. The closing praise of Allah is the cure: the spotlight belongs to Him, as does all grandeur.

outline.heading: The cluster's third warning: arrogance
outline.gist: After advice on dawah and a warning against materialism and taking things lightly, this surah warns that vanity and arrogance are lethal.

outline.heading: Signs in the heavens and the earth
outline.gist: The surah lists Allah's signs and asks what else people will believe in if not these.

outline.heading: From faith to certainty to understanding
outline.gist: Each sign-verse ends on a higher state, showing how reflection builds faith step by step.

outline.heading: Group one: the disbeliever who lies knowingly
outline.gist: He hears the signs, turns away in arrogance because the truth does not serve his interest, and mocks them.

outline.heading: Group two: believers, for whom everything was made subservient
outline.gist: The cosmos was created to serve you, which should lead to reflection, not pride.

outline.heading: Tell the believers to forgive
outline.gist: Allah will handle reward and punishment; using Islam as a tool of arrogance toward non-Muslims is one of the worst things a Muslim can do.

outline.heading: Holding firmly to the shari'ah
outline.gist: The Children of Israel were given clarity and discarded it; the Prophet is told to follow the clear way and not the whims of those who do not know.

outline.heading: Cherry-picking the deen opens cracks for arrogance
outline.gist: Following only the parts we like unbalances our faith, and arrogance and vanity seep in through the cracks.

outline.heading: Group three: knowledge with desire as one's god
outline.gist: Anyone with knowledge risks following their own whims, being led astray despite knowing, and concluding life is only living and dying.

outline.heading: Educated people losing faith today
outline.gist: Never have so many knowledgeable people lost faith in a supreme power as now.

outline.heading: Group four: every nation on its knees
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment whole nations kneel and are called to their book; there is group accountability as well as individual.

outline.heading: Humble now or humble then
outline.gist: Kneeling is humility that nation lacked in this world; everyone will be humbled, the only choice is when.

outline.heading: Societies judged for leaving the weak behind
outline.gist: What societies do through arrogance is abandon the poor and vulnerable, and they will answer for it as groups.

outline.heading: Praise as the cure for vanity
outline.gist: Saying al-hamdu lillah moves the spotlight off ourselves; it was never on us.

outline.heading: All grandeur belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Supremacy is His right alone; we cannot even sustain our own bodies, and every group must beware of arrogance.

6:161.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّنِي هَدَىٰنِي رَبِّيٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ دِينࣰ ا قِيَمࣰ ا مِّلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
6:161.en: Say: Lo! As for me, my Lord hath guided me unto a straight path, a right religion, the community of Abraham, the upright, who was no idolater

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

111:1.en: The power of Abu Lahab will perish, and he will perish

29:45.ar: ٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِۗ وَلَذِكۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَصۡنَعُونَ
29:45.en: Recite that which hath been inspired in thee of the Scripture, and establish worship. Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity, but verily remembrance of Allah is more important. And Allah knoweth what ye do

41:30.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَقَٰمُواْ تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ وَأَبۡشِرُواْ بِٱلۡجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي كُنتُمۡ تُوعَدُونَ
41:30.en: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised

4:105.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِتَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَا تَكُن لِّلۡخَآئِنِينَ خَصِيمࣰ ا
4:105.en: Lo! We reveal unto thee the Scripture with the truth, that thou mayst judge between mankind by that which Allah showeth thee. And be not thou a pleader for the treacherous

90:11.en: But he hath not attempted the Ascent

90:12.en: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the Ascent is

90:14.ar: أَوۡ إِطۡعَٰمࣱ فِي يَوۡمࣲ ذِي مَسۡغَبَةࣲ‏
90:14.en: And to feed in the day of hunger

90:16.en: Or some poor wretch in misery

efXCFLphluA.speaker: adnan
efXCFLphluA.speaker_note: fifth episode of his own series, refers to his earlier episodes and his own practice
efXCFLphluA.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 5: Values and Behaviours
efXCFLphluA.one_line: Behaviours are only the visible output of values; to change how we act we must trace each behaviour back and repair the value behind it.
efXCFLphluA.summary: The sheikh lays out a chain: values, which are convictions we tag as right or wrong, generate ethics, and ethics generate behaviours. Islam is a religion of upright values, and the Prophet said people are like minerals whose best qualities carry into Islam. Through examples he shows that how consistently someone acts depends on how deeply they understand a value. Honesty has reasoned exceptions, compassion is absolute even toward enemies, lying reveals a belief that honesty is optional, and struggling to lower the gaze reflects half-conviction rather than weakness. Anger at a child who refuses to memorise Quran shows several defective values firing at once. Collectively, Muslims hold a fatalistic belief that nothing will change, and Abu Lahab is named in the Quran because wealth was his ultimate value. Rituals are not values but are generated by them and reinforce them; prayer rests on dozens of convictions. He lists Islamic values such as justice, incorruptibility, trustworthiness, compassion, avoiding harm, objectivity and following evidence, illustrated by the Prophet returning trusts to those expelling him and by the Quran defending a wrongly accused Jewish man. Values must be constants, not moods. His action plan is to observe your own behaviours this Ramadan, trace each to its value, and rethink that value until it holds steady.

outline.heading: Values generate ethics, ethics generate behaviours
outline.gist: A value is a conviction tagged right or wrong; we see only behaviours, which are its consequences.

outline.heading: Islam as a religion of upright values (6:161, 30:30)
outline.gist: The straight path and the upright religion are built on values.

outline.heading: People are like minerals
outline.gist: Those with the best values before Islam are the best in Islam once they learn it properly.

outline.heading: Honesty: value, ethic, behaviour
outline.gist: How consistently you are honest depends on how deeply you have understood and thought through the value.

outline.heading: Reasoned exceptions to honesty
outline.gist: Truth in war or a harsh truth to a loved one does not serve honesty's purpose.

outline.heading: Behaviours reflect values; start with yourself
outline.gist: Before reacting to a child's behaviour, find the value behind it, and do this for yourself first.

outline.heading: Compassion as an absolute value
outline.gist: Everyone, even an enemy, deserves mercy, and that should show in behaviour.

outline.heading: Why people lie
outline.gist: Lying comes from believing honesty is for family and friends but not for getting ahead.

outline.heading: Lowering the gaze is a conviction problem
outline.gist: Struggling with it is not weakness but half-belief that looking at haram harms you or matters to Allah.

outline.heading: Anger as several values firing at once
outline.gist: A father explodes when his son refuses to memorise Quran because family control, parenting success and others' opinions are all triggered.

outline.heading: Revising the defective values
outline.gist: Children will struggle with faith as you did, and caring what people say is a value to discard.

outline.heading: The ummah's fatalism
outline.gist: Believing nothing will ever change and everything is a conspiracy produces inaction.

outline.heading: Abu Lahab: wealth as the ultimate value
outline.gist: Though once close to the Prophet, he opposed him because the message threatened his trade.

outline.heading: We teach behaviours before values
outline.gist: Values are instilled through experience and mentorship, not lectures.

outline.heading: What made you do this?
outline.gist: The Prophet asked people why they acted; punishment can force a person to revise values, as with cheating in exams.

outline.heading: Success at any cost
outline.gist: Breaking rules to get ahead manifests a value that success comes first.

outline.heading: Rituals are generated by values
outline.gist: Prayer reinforces values and rests on dozens of convictions; a child who does not pray lacks them, not just discipline.

outline.heading: Values of Islam: righteousness, justice, incorruptibility (41:30)
outline.gist: Creation rests on truth, justice must always be upheld, and believers stay steadfast.

outline.heading: Trustworthiness: returning trusts at the Hijrah
outline.gist: The Prophet left Ali behind to return the possessions of the very people expelling him.

outline.heading: Compassion, avoiding harm, courage, moderation
outline.gist: Not causing harm became so strong a value it turned into a legal maxim.

outline.heading: Objectivity, open-mindedness, following evidence
outline.gist: Rejecting the new, denying benefit of the doubt and refusing to admit error are defective values.

outline.heading: Leave it, it is rotten: tribal calls
outline.gist: The Prophet reacted strongly to tribalism and collective arrogance because they expose a defective value.

outline.heading: Abu Dharr and Bilal
outline.gist: Insulting Bilal's lineage showed a trace of jahiliyyah, and Abu Dharr hurried to apologise.

outline.heading: The stolen shield and the Jewish man (4:105)
outline.gist: Revelation cleared a falsely accused Jewish man because justice is absolute regardless of faith or tribe.

outline.heading: Values are constants: the steep path (90:11-16)
outline.gist: Freeing captives and feeding the hungry even when you are poor shows a value is real.

outline.heading: How to instil values: watch yourself
outline.gist: Values are rebuilt through deep thought and mindfulness of your own behaviour.

outline.heading: That's just how I am
outline.gist: Difficulty expressing emotion or arguing with a spouse comes from unrevised values.

outline.heading: Taking others' spots and scattering shoes at Jumuah
outline.gist: These reflect a missing value that others' right to be there equals mine, and a missing value of keeping the masjid clean.

outline.heading: A skeleton of incoherent practice
outline.gist: Fasting to feel others' hunger then overeating, and rushing the imam at night, show values and behaviours no longer align.

outline.heading: Without values, the behaviours go too
outline.gist: You will only pray so long without values; strengthen why you pray.

outline.heading: Action plan: trace behaviours back to values
outline.gist: Observe how honest, respectful and trustworthy you are, then study and rethink the value behind each behaviour.

outline.heading: Only the prophets have perfect values; aim for steadfastness
outline.gist: Constant revision produces steadfastness, so people know you will always be honest and kind.

outline.heading: Reprogramming your life
outline.gist: Fixing small defects in your value set is like debugging a program.

outline.heading: Outro

3:103.en: And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate. And remember Allah's favour unto you: How ye were enemies and He made friendship between your hearts so that ye became as brothers by His grace; and (how) ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire, and He did save you from it. 2:285.en: The messenger believeth in that which hath been revealed unto him from his Lord and (so do) believers. 43:32.en: Is it they who apportion thy Lord's mercy? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of the world, and raised some of them above others in rank that some of them may take labour from others; and the mercy of thy Lord is better than (the wealth) that they amass

-MGoqn6Mv5A.summary: The sheikh argues that two neglected practices, networking and mentorship, could dissolve many of the community's problems. Allah made humanity diverse so people would know one another, and joined believers' hearts into brotherhood. He dwells on the Prophet's pairing of Makkan emigrants with Madinan helpers in their homes, a striking feat given their different lineages, dialects and livelihoods, and contrasts it with the alternative of separate neighbourhoods. Integration brought problems but built bonds no money could buy. Mentorship rests on Surat al-Asr: people win back time by advising one another, a two-way exchange. The Prophet was himself mentored, including by the prophets he met during the Ascension, with Musa sending him back to reduce the prayers. The right stance toward teachers is to hear and accept revelation while asking them to listen and give time. Today we invest in buildings and possessions rather than people. The Prophet knew each companion, rode with Mu'adh, included the young Ibn Abbas, and corrected al-Fadl gently. Youth lack role models and practical skills, which come from close companionship with scholars. His action plan: build a network of skilled Muslim professionals, reach the many Muslims who never attend, find a mentor at any age, and mentor younger people, starting with teenagers in your own family.

outline.heading: Why networking and mentorship matter
outline.gist: Two topics that sound minor but in which the community invests far too little.

outline.heading: Created diverse so we may know one another (49:13)
outline.gist: Nations, tribes and cultures exist so people get to know and learn from each other.

outline.heading: Hold together; hearts joined into brotherhood (3:103)
outline.gist: Allah turned former enemies into brothers through His favour.

outline.heading: One body, greeting strangers and kinship ties
outline.gist: Believers are like one body; feed the needy, greet those you know and do not know, and keep family ties.

outline.heading: The brotherhood pact: how different Makkah and Madinah were
outline.gist: Different lineage, dialect and livelihood made housing emigrants with the Ansar a remarkable experiment.

outline.heading: Arabia amazed by the brotherhood
outline.gist: People came to see whether Makkans really lived in Madinan homes; the brotherhood is historically unparalleled.

outline.heading: Hearts joined that money could not buy (8:63)
outline.gist: Love of Allah, not wealth, brought the two groups together.

outline.heading: The alternative: a separate Makkan neighbourhood
outline.gist: Isolated enclaves would have produced two Muslim societies and lost brotherhood and networking.

outline.heading: Integrate, then deal with the difficulties
outline.gist: Bringing different people together causes problems, but its value to the community is far greater.

outline.heading: Mentorship in Surat al-Asr (103:1-3)
outline.gist: Humans are in constant loss of time except those who believe, act and counsel one another.

outline.heading: Advice as a two-way road
outline.gist: Giving and accepting advice saves each other time by sharing failures and experience.

outline.heading: Why parents hate their children repeating their mistakes
outline.gist: Parents want children to take their experience instead of relearning it.

outline.heading: The Prophet mentored by the prophets on the Ascension
outline.gist: He met Adam, Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa and Ibrahim; Musa coached him to seek fewer prayers.

outline.heading: Hear and obey, and ask teachers to listen (2:285, 4:46)
outline.gist: Instead of 'we hear and disobey', accept revelation fully while asking teachers to listen to your concerns and give you time.

outline.heading: We no longer invest in people
outline.gist: We invest in places and possessions; transformation only comes from investing in human beings.

outline.heading: The Prophet knew each companion individually
outline.gist: He knew their names, prayed for them and listened to their problems; they were not a herd.

outline.heading: Mu'adh on the donkey and young Ibn Abbas
outline.gist: He told Mu'adh he loved him and taught him, and kept the young Ibn Abbas in gatherings, treating him like an adult.

outline.heading: Correcting al-Fadl gently
outline.gist: The Prophet turned al-Fadl's face away when he stared at a young woman, teaching without words.

outline.heading: Ibn Wahb: one year of knowledge, nineteen of manners
outline.gist: Ibn Wahb spent most of his twenty years with Imam Malik learning how to behave.

outline.heading: Who are our youth's idols?
outline.gist: TV idols, artists and athletes have replaced Muslim role models worth emulating.

outline.heading: Teaching by example and close companionship
outline.gist: The Prophet taught by doing; staying close to a scholar for a week teaches more than years of academic study.

outline.heading: Information without skills
outline.gist: Youth lack social, financial, political, religious and personal skills that only one-on-one coaching builds.

outline.heading: Supporting one another as a jama'ah
outline.gist: Within a like-minded community you back others' work morally, socially and financially even without joining it.

outline.heading: How many people at your masjid do you know?
outline.gist: Initiatives get duplicated because we do not know each other; most people know only their own bubble.

outline.heading: Made different to benefit one another (43:32)
outline.gist: Knowing people removes animosity and suspicion, since it is hard to resent someone you know.

outline.heading: Networking brings like-minded people together
outline.gist: People with shared interests can work together instead of wasting effort separately.

outline.heading: Each generation is responsible for the next
outline.gist: He speaks because many elders invested in him, and now owes the same to those after him.

outline.heading: You only need to be ten steps ahead
outline.gist: No need to be a scholar; if every young adult mentored five or six youths, communities would change.

outline.heading: The brotherhood pact was also mentorship
outline.gist: The Madinan offered a home, the Makkan offered years of learning from the Prophet.

outline.heading: Get your teenagers a mentor
outline.gist: Youth often listen to others' advice more readily than their parents'.

outline.heading: Action plan: build an Islamic network
outline.gist: Get to know people and introduce them to others to create a network of skilled, forward-thinking professionals.

outline.heading: Reaching the Muslims who never come
outline.gist: Of tens of thousands of Muslims in the city, a few hundred engage; we need to know and serve the rest and mentor their youth.

outline.heading: Village networking vs North American cities
outline.gist: In his Syrian village everyone knew each other; in cities it must be built deliberately, as businesses do.

outline.heading: Find a mentor
outline.gist: Everyone who achieves anything had a mentor, and he was mentored by his father and teachers.

outline.heading: Mentor someone, starting with family
outline.gist: Invite younger relatives over, get to know them and mentor them, while finding your own mentor.

WFgoamGL9Hs.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 1: Leadership and Followship
WFgoamGL9Hs.one_line: In Islam leadership and followship are nearly the same thing: know your position, fulfil your role, follow wisely and hold leaders accountable.
WFgoamGL9Hs.summary: Opening a series on rethinking habits that hold the community back, the sheikh argues that leadership and followship are almost synonymous in Islam. He defines leadership as recognising your position, doing your role as well as you can and helping others do theirs. From the Quran he draws humanity's stewardship, Ibrahim made an imam on merit rather than lineage, the believers' prayer to lead the pious, and Dawud as the first named khalifah. The Prophet himself followed Ibrahim while raising leaders among his companions. He calls Jumuah the system Islam built for leadership and wants it revived as a place where the community's leader gives direction. Good leaders need vision, personal example, social intelligence and self-control. Good followship is not blind: the Prophet consulted, followed the majority, accepted correction at Badr, and no one is obeyed in disobedience to Allah. Followers must care about the community, trust qualified leaders and hold them accountable. A population becomes a community by centralising social, financial, political or religious leadership, and religious leadership is the most achievable for Muslims in Canada. He asks each listener to locate their position, lead those behind and follow those ahead, demand vision, and stop leaving vulnerable people behind.

outline.heading: Why rethink our behaviour now
outline.gist: Staying home during the pandemic is a chance to reflect and return to something more beneficial.

outline.heading: Islam is rooted in reform; this world is the vehicle
outline.gist: Islam refuses stagnation, and if we lose control of this world we will not reach our destination.

outline.heading: Defining leadership
outline.gist: Leadership is knowing where you stand, doing your role as well as you can and helping others do theirs; not everyone is at the podium.

outline.heading: Humanity as steward of the earth (2:30)
outline.gist: A khalifah is responsible for something on behalf of someone else, a role given to every human.

outline.heading: Ibrahim made an imam: merit, not bloodline (2:124)
outline.gist: Allah tells Ibrahim the oppressors among his descendants will not lead.

outline.heading: Praying to be leaders of the pious (25:74)
outline.gist: Believers ask Allah to make them leaders for the righteous, so aspiring to lead is part of faith.

outline.heading: Dawud, the first named khalifah (38:26)
outline.gist: Dawud led on every level, as prophet, king, judge and commander, and was told to judge with justice.

outline.heading: The Prophet as follower and maker of leaders
outline.gist: He followed Ibrahim, gave new Muslims leadership roles, yet told Abu Dharr not to lead even two people, showing piety alone does not qualify someone.

outline.heading: Jumuah as Islam's system of leadership
outline.gist: Jumuah lost its significance when leadership was removed; it should be given by the community's leader, who sets direction weekly.

outline.heading: Leadership attribute: vision
outline.gist: A leader needs a practical vision that serves people; leading without one is driving blindfolded.

outline.heading: Leadership attribute: leading by example
outline.gist: People trusted the Prophet because they saw him working harder than anyone.

outline.heading: Leadership attribute: social intelligence
outline.gist: Leaders must understand and communicate with people to be effective.

outline.heading: Leadership attribute: self-control
outline.gist: Leaders must respond to crises with calm and steadiness rather than emotion.

outline.heading: Negative followship: Pharaoh's people
outline.gist: Pharaoh was a strong leader with an evil direction, and his careless people followed him to ruin.

outline.heading: The pledge to listen and obey
outline.gist: The people of Madinah agreed to obey the Prophet whether or not they fully agreed.

outline.heading: Followship is never blind
outline.gist: The Prophet consulted, accepted correction on the camp at Badr, went out to Uhud by majority, and no one is obeyed in disobeying Allah.

outline.heading: Followship defined: a two-way road
outline.gist: Lead those behind you and follow those ahead while questioning them; the companions followed Abu Bakr then Umar without resentment.

outline.heading: Followship need: caring about the community
outline.gist: Praying Jumuah and leaving without caring about the community's state must change.

outline.heading: Followship need: trusting your leadership
outline.gist: Trust qualified, service-oriented leaders and follow even when you do not fully agree, or change them.

outline.heading: Followship need: holding leaders accountable
outline.gist: Unquestioned leaders grow lazy and drift toward dictatorship, so followers must check progress toward the vision.

outline.heading: From population to community
outline.gist: London's Muslims are a population until they centralise leadership in one of four domains.

outline.heading: Domain: social leadership
outline.gist: Living and socialising in one area, like a Little Italy or Chinatown, which is hard for Muslims here.

outline.heading: Domain: financial leadership
outline.gist: Pooling wealth into one fund that meets community needs, difficult but achievable.

outline.heading: Domain: political leadership
outline.gist: The hardest of the four for Muslims in Canada.

outline.heading: Domain: religious leadership
outline.gist: The most sustainable and obtainable, since Allah already gave us Jumuah and a model of leading and following.

outline.heading: The best leader is the best follower of the Prophet
outline.gist: Accept not being at the front, lead within your capacity and follow the group's leadership.

outline.heading: Why our communities spin in circles
outline.gist: Without effective leadership and followship the same quarrels repeat year after year, in London and everywhere.

outline.heading: Action plan: find your coordinates
outline.gist: Identify where you stand in your society, whether at the front or the middle.

outline.heading: All of you are shepherds
outline.gist: Everyone leads within their sphere, the man in his family and the woman in her home, and is accountable for it.

outline.heading: Demand vision and hold leaders to it
outline.gist: Find a leader where you are not one, require direction, and hold them accountable; revive Jumuah.

outline.heading: The people we leave behind
outline.gist: People with mental illness or disabilities, elders, immigrants, the poor and the spiritually needy are underserved because of this failure.

outline.heading: Outro

28:77.ar: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:77.en: But seek the abode of the Hereafter in that which Allah hath given thee and neglect not thy portion of the world, and be thou kind even as Allah hath been kind to thee, and seek not corruption in the earth; lo! Allah loveth not corrupters

28:78.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةࣰ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ

hguPptCD0yE.title: The Empty Space Ep. 6: The Sins and Solutions
hguPptCD0yE.one_line: Three of the four major diseases of the heart, vanity, arrogance and showing off, and their cures through praise, forgiveness-seeking and exalting Allah.
hguPptCD0yE.summary: He turns to the major diseases of the heart, which every faith tradition names, and covers three. Vanity is crediting yourself for success; he walks through how family, health, intellect, curiosity and circumstance were all handed to you, so honest gratitude means saying Allah enabled it, while others should credit your effort. Its cure is alhamdulillah lived with the mind, and its opposite is confidence, not self-erasure. Qarun, who claimed his wealth came from his own knowledge, is the warning. Arrogance needs comparison, yet no one knows another person's starting hand; a person who escapes abuse and poverty may outrank us. Iblis's 'I am better' is its root, humility is simply realism about one's own sins, and the cure is istighfar that keeps you busy with your own flaws. Two stories drive this home: the sinner and the worshipper on the mountain, and a scholar's dream of Shaytan's hooks. Showing off is seeking people's gaze; enjoying praise is not riya, and feedback still matters, but only Allah's opinion should count. Its cure is exalting Allah until people's praise feels small. He urges working on all three together and not abandoning deeds over imperfect intentions.

outline.heading: Opening
The four major diseases of the heart
outline.gist: Fixing the four main diseases weakens all the others; every faith tradition has named them.

outline.heading: Vanity defined
outline.gist: Believing your own effort is the reason for success; the aim is to shrink an inflated ego to healthy confidence.

outline.heading: The building blocks of success were handed to you
outline.gist: Nurturing parents, health, intellect, curiosity and fortunate circumstances made your effort possible, and none of them were earned.

outline.heading: Changing the narrative from 'I did' to 'Allah enabled'
outline.gist: Allah already promised to reward and praise your small participation, so the praise belongs to Him.

outline.heading: The cure for vanity: alhamdulillah with the mind
outline.gist: Honestly acknowledge how minimal your part was; he applies it to his own teaching as a blessing rather than an accomplishment.

outline.heading: Confidence, not humility, is the opposite of vanity
outline.gist: Hold the middle of the pendulum between vanity and worthlessness, confident that Allah believes in you.

outline.heading: Qarun: 'I was given it because of my knowledge'
outline.gist: His people urged him to enjoy his wealth without vanity, but he credited his own skill.

outline.heading: Others credit your effort; you credit Allah
outline.gist: Society should praise people's contribution, but the person himself must see it as Allah's gift; Qarun was swallowed by the earth.

outline.heading: You do not own even yourself
outline.gist: Body, spirit and earth belong to Allah, so the good you do with them is His too.

outline.heading: Room for our bodies, not our egos
outline.gist: Living by constant praise of Allah shrinks the ego to the right size while the heart grows.

outline.heading: Arrogance defined
outline.gist: Arrogance compares and feels superior, leading to rejecting truth and refusing to admit error.

outline.heading: No one knows another's starting point
outline.gist: There is no agreed criterion and only Allah judges; even siblings do not know the hand the other was dealt.

outline.heading: Iblis: 'I am better than him'
outline.gist: The nafs invents bogus reasons for superiority, as Iblis did with fire and clay.

outline.heading: Humility is acknowledging reality
outline.gist: The only sins you know are your own, so judging others uses knowledge you do not have.

outline.heading: The cure for arrogance: istighfar
outline.gist: Seeking forgiveness keeps you busy with your own flaws, leaving no time to spot others'.

outline.heading: The person from a broken home may be better than you
outline.gist: Someone who escapes abuse, war and addiction to live decently has done more with their hand; do not judge the beggar.

outline.heading: The sinner and the worshipper on the mountain
outline.gist: Each avoided the other's path; the humble sinner was guided and the self-satisfied worshipper was not.

outline.heading: The scholar's dream of Shaytan's hooks
outline.gist: The biggest hook was for a humble man arranging shoes; the famous scholar needed none because he was already ahead of Shaytan.

outline.heading: An atom of arrogance and avoiding inferiority
outline.gist: Arrogance bars entry to Jannah, but the goal is to stop comparing, not to swing to self-hatred; al-Ghazali's way of seeing others as better.

outline.heading: Servants have no ego
outline.gist: The Prophet sought forgiveness a hundred times daily despite his rank; greatness belongs to Allah alone, and dropping comparison brings happiness.

outline.heading: Showing off defined; sincerity as its opposite
outline.gist: Riya seeks people's gaze and eats good deeds from within like a termite; ikhlas is the core of the deen.

outline.heading: Enjoying praise is not riya
outline.gist: Appreciation is glad tidings and children need it to grow, but overpraising makes sincerity harder.

outline.heading: Indifferent to praise, open to feedback
outline.gist: Do the right thing regardless of reactions while still seeking feedback; people's approval is fleeting and Allah needs no partners.

outline.heading: Only Allah gives status and strength
outline.gist: Teach the nafs that people's eyes cannot give it what it wants.

outline.heading: The cure for showing off: exalting Allah
outline.gist: Riya stems from not seeing Allah as infinitely greater than people; magnifying Him makes their opinion small.

outline.heading: Teaching sincerity at the right age
outline.gist: Teenagers are motivated by others' esteem; the work on riya begins in one's twenties.

outline.heading: The diseases are intertwined; treat them together
outline.gist: Vanity, arrogance and riya feed each other, so fight them all at once with tasbih and asking Allah to accept.

outline.heading: Sincerity is a lifelong journey
outline.gist: Do not abandon a deed over mixed intentions; admit the impurity and keep working on it, remembering everyone is equally weak.

outline.heading: Outro
Proper perspectives take time
outline.gist: Many diseases fade once the right principles sink in through continued learning and examples.

42:8.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَهُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَلَٰكِن يُدۡخِلُ مَن يَشَآءُ فِي رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ وَٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَا لَهُم مِّن وَلِيࣲّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ
42:8.en: Had Allah willed, He could have made them one community, but Allah bringeth whom He will into His mercy. And the wrong-doers have no friend nor helper

42:9.ar: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَۖ فَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلۡوَلِيُّ وَهُوَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
42:9.en: Or have they chosen protecting friends besides Him? But Allah, He (alone) is the Protecting Friend. He quickeneth the dead, and He is Able to do all things

42:10.ar: وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفۡتُمۡ فِيهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فَحُكۡمُهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُ وَإِلَيۡهِ أُنِيبُ
42:10.en: And in whatsoever ye differ, the verdict therein belongeth to Allah. Such is my Lord, in Whom I put my trust, and unto Whom I turn

42:11.ar: فَاطِرُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا يَذۡرَؤُكُمۡ فِيهِۚ لَيۡسَ كَمِثۡلِهِۦ شَيۡءࣱۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
42:11.en: The Creator of the heavens and the earth. He hath made for you pairs of yourselves, and of the cattle also pairs, whereby He multiplieth you. Naught is as His likeness; and He is the Hearer, the Seer

42:12.ar: لَهُۥ مَقَالِيدُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
42:12.en: His are the keys of the heavens and the earth. He enlargeth providence for whom He will and straiteneth (it for whom He will). Lo! He is Knower of all things

42:13.ar: ۞شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِۦ نُوحࣰ ا وَٱلَّذِيٓ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَا وَصَّيۡنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓۖ أَنۡ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُواْ فِيهِۚ كَبُرَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ مَا تَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِۚ ٱللَّهُ يَجۡتَبِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ مَن يُنِيبُ
42:13.en: He hath ordained for you that religion which He commended unto Noah, and that which We inspire in thee (Muhammad), and that which We commended unto Abraham and Moses and Jesus, saying: Establish the religion, and be not divided therein. Dreadful for the idolaters is that unto which thou callest them. Allah chooseth for Himself whom He will, and guideth unto Himself him who turneth (toward Him)

42:14.ar: وَمَا تَفَرَّقُوٓاْ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡعِلۡمُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ وَلَوۡلَا كَلِمَةࣱ سَبَقَتۡ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى لَّقُضِيَ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُورِثُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ لَفِي شَكࣲّ مِّنۡهُ مُرِيبࣲ‏
42:14.en: And they were not divided until after the knowledge came unto them, through rivalry among themselves; and had it not been for a Word that had already gone forth from thy Lord for an appointed term, it surely had been judged between them. And those who were made to inherit the Scripture after them are verily in hopeless doubt concerning it

42:15.ar: فَلِذَٰلِكَ فَٱدۡعُۖ وَٱسۡتَقِمۡ كَمَآ أُمِرۡتَۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعۡ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۖ وَقُلۡ ءَامَنتُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن كِتَٰبࣲۖ وَأُمِرۡتُ لِأَعۡدِلَ بَيۡنَكُمُۖ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمۡۖ لَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡۖ لَا حُجَّةَ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمُۖ ٱللَّهُ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
42:15.en: Unto this, then, summon (O Muhammad). And be thou upright as thou art commanded, and follow not their lusts, but say: I believe in whatever scripture Allah hath sent down, and I am commanded to be just among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. Unto us our works and unto you your works; no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and unto Him is the journeying

42:20.ar: مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرۡثَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ نَزِدۡ لَهُۥ فِي حَرۡثِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرۡثَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَا وَمَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِن نَّصِيبٍ
42:20.en: Whoso desireth the harvest of the Hereafter, We give him increase in its harvest. And whoso desireth the harvest of the world, We give him thereof, and he hath no portion in the Hereafter

42:21.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ شُرَكَٰٓؤُاْ شَرَعُواْ لَهُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا لَمۡ يَأۡذَنۢ بِهِ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَوۡلَا كَلِمَةُ ٱلۡفَصۡلِ لَقُضِيَ بَيۡنَهُمۡۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
42:21.en: Or have they partners (of Allah) who have made lawful for them in religion that which Allah allowed not? And but for a decisive word (gone forth already), it would have been judged between them. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom

42:22.ar: تَرَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا كَسَبُواْ وَهُوَ وَاقِعُۢ بِهِمۡۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فِي رَوۡضَاتِ ٱلۡجَنَّاتِۖ لَهُم مَّا يَشَآءُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَضۡلُ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ
42:22.en: Thou seest the wrong-doers fearful of that which they have earned, and it will surely befall them, while those who believe and do good works (will be) in flowering meadows of the Gardens, having what they wish from their Lord. This is the great preferment

42:23.ar: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ ٱللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِۗ قُل لَّآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًا إِلَّا ٱلۡمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰۗ وَمَن يَقۡتَرِفۡ حَسَنَةࣰ نَّزِدۡ لَهُۥ فِيهَا حُسۡنًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ شَكُورٌ
42:23.en: This it is which Allah announceth unto His bondmen who believe and do good works. Say (O Muhammad, unto mankind): I ask of you no fee therefor, save lovingkindness among kinsfolk. And whoso scoreth a good deed We add unto its good for him. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Responsive

42:36.ar: فَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَمَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
42:36.en: Now whatever ye have been given is but a passing comfort for the life of the world, and that which Allah hath is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord

42:37.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُواْ هُمۡ يَغۡفِرُونَ
42:37.en: And those who shun the worst of sins and indecencies and, when they are wroth, forgive

42:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَمۡرُهُمۡ شُورَىٰ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
42:38.en: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them

42:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلۡبَغۡيُ هُمۡ يَنتَصِرُونَ
42:39.en: And those who, when great wrong is done to them, defend themselves

42:42.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَظۡلِمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ وَيَبۡغُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
42:42.en: The way (of blame) is only against those who oppress mankind, and wrongfully rebel in the earth. For such there is a painful doom

42:48.ar: فَإِنۡ أَعۡرَضُواْ فَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَفِيظًاۖ إِنۡ عَلَيۡكَ إِلَّا ٱلۡبَلَٰغُۗ وَإِنَّآ إِذَآ أَذَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِنَّا رَحۡمَةࣰ فَرِحَ بِهَاۖ وَإِن تُصِبۡهُمۡ سَيِّئَةُۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ فَإِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ كَفُورࣱ‏
42:48.en: But if they are averse, We have not sent thee as a warder over them. Thine is only to convey (the message). And lo! when We cause man to taste of mercy from Us he exulteth therefor. And if some evil striketh them because of that which their own hands have sent before, then lo! man is an ingrate

42:49.ar: لِّلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَٰثࣰ ا وَيَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ ٱلذُّكُورَ
42:49.en: Unto Allah belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. He createth what He will. He bestoweth female (offspring) upon whom He will, and bestoweth male (offspring) upon whom He will

42:50.ar: أَوۡ يُزَوِّجُهُمۡ ذُكۡرَانࣰ ا وَإِنَٰثࣰ اۖ وَيَجۡعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيمًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمࣱ قَدِيرࣱ‏
42:50.en: Or He mingleth them, males and females, and He maketh barren whom He will. Lo! He is Knower, Powerful

42:51.ar: ۞وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحۡيًا أَوۡ مِن وَرَآيِٕ حِجَابٍ أَوۡ يُرۡسِلَ رَسُولࣰ ا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذۡنِهِۦ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيٌّ حَكِيمࣱ‏
42:51.en: And it was not (vouchsafed) to any mortal that Allah should speak to him unless (it be) by revelation or from behind a veil, or (that) He sendeth a messenger to reveal what He will by His leave. Lo! He is Exalted, Wise

42:52.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ رُوحࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَمۡرِنَاۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدۡرِي مَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ وَلَا ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ وَلَٰكِن جَعَلۡنَٰهُ نُورࣰ ا نَّهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَاۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهۡدِيٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
42:52.en: And thus have We inspired in thee (Muhammad) a Spirit of Our command. Thou knewest not what the Scripture was, nor what the Faith. But We have made it a light whereby We guide whom We will of Our bondmen. And lo! thou verily dost guide unto a right path

42:53.ar: صِرَٰطِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ أَلَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
42:53.en: The path of Allah, unto Whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Do not all things reach Allah at last

a9L20S9A7U8.title: Surat Ash-Shura Summary
a9L20S9A7U8.one_line: Ash-Shura teaches that difference is Allah's design but division is forbidden: consult the like-minded, deal fairly with others, convey and let go.
a9L20S9A7U8.summary: In alternating English and Arabic he places Ash-Shura third among the Hawamim, which advise those calling to Allah. After Ghafir's call with trust and dua and Fussilat's call by action, Ash-Shura addresses difference. Allah chose not to make people one nation; difference in looks, languages, opinions and references is the norm of creation, and disputes are referred back to Allah's judgment, who Himself is unlike anything. Every prophet from Nuh to Muhammad was given one command: establish the religion and do not split over it. He separates difference, which is natural, from division, which means refusing to hear, work with or deal kindly with others, and turning them into enemies. The Prophet asked only for affection due to kinship, a bond we share with all children of Adam. The qualities of believers to gather around you include faith, reliance on Allah, avoiding major sins, forgiving when angry, prayer, shura among themselves, and resisting oppression. Shura was taught in Mecca and saved the Muslims at the Trench, but it only works among people who share foundations; working in separate groups toward the same goal is not division. The fault lies only with oppressors, and our duty is to convey. He asks Muslims to build teams of like-minded people while treating others with respect.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: calling those who argue and won't listen
outline.gist: Ghafir taught calling with dua; Fussilat that some will never listen however clear you are, so call by action.

outline.heading: Surround yourself with the like-minded and consult
outline.gist: The surah's name means consultation, an early form of what democracy aims at; consult people who share your outlook and move forward.

outline.heading: Had Allah willed, one nation
outline.gist: Hold on to your references with pride while dealing well with those who differ; Allah chose not to make people one nation.

outline.heading: Whatever you differ in, its judgment is with Allah
outline.gist: Disputes are referred back to Allah, the Supreme, who is unlike us.

outline.heading: The Hawamim: advice for callers to Allah
outline.gist: Ghafir: entrust and supplicate; Fussilat: action speaks louder; Ash-Shura: the law of difference in creation.

outline.heading: Difference is Allah's will, not a mistake
outline.gist: No two people are identical; we gather with the like-minded, stay firm on our references and call others kindly. He made us nations and tribes.

outline.heading: Nothing is like Him
outline.gist: When we differ we return to Allah's ruling; the greater difference is between us and Allah, and any likeness is only figurative.

outline.heading: One religion ordained for every prophet
outline.gist: He recites the passage on what was ordained for Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad, and the command to call and stay upright.

outline.heading: Establish the religion and do not split: difference versus division
outline.gist: Difference in looks, languages and opinions is natural; division is refusing to hear, work with or deal with others, and treating them as enemies.

outline.heading: Division came after knowledge, out of envy; stay upright
outline.gist: After their prophets died people split through aggression. Continue calling, stay upright and ignore people with agendas.

outline.heading: No argument between us and you
outline.gist: Believe in every revealed book and be just; they have their deeds and we have ours, with no need for enmity.

outline.heading: Harvest of the Hereafter or of this world
outline.gist: He introduces the verses on the two harvests and the affection due to kinship.

outline.heading: We differ even in what we want
outline.gist: Some sow for the Hereafter and some for this world; each is given, but a harvest taken here may be missing there. No one can be forced.

outline.heading: Only affection due to kinship
outline.gist: The Prophet asked Quraysh for no wage, only regard for kinship; with non-Muslims too we are one family, children of Adam and Hawwa.

outline.heading: Love of the Prophet's family
outline.gist: Another valid meaning is respect for the Prophet's household, which deserves more attention. Whatever you are given is passing enjoyment.

outline.heading: The qualities of the believers
outline.gist: He recites the description of those who believe, rely on Allah, avoid major sins, forgive when angry, pray, consult and spend.

outline.heading: Avoiding major sins; forgiving in anger
outline.gist: The people to surround yourself with share outlines of behaviour: avoiding the major sins and indecencies, and forgiving when angered.

outline.heading: Their affairs by consultation: the Trench
outline.gist: Responding to Allah and praying, then shura; unilateral decisions end in catastrophe, while consultation over the trench saved the Muslims.

outline.heading: Going separate ways without enmity
outline.gist: Groups that differ may work separately toward the same goal; division begins only when they become enemies. When wronged, believers defend themselves.

outline.heading: Faith, reliance and conduct
outline.gist: The listed qualities span the heart (faith and reliance) and behaviour (avoiding sins, forgiving).

outline.heading: Shura in a Meccan surah; refusing oppression
outline.gist: The Prophet taught consultation before Medina and practised it there; believers do not stay silent when wronged.

outline.heading: Consultation needs shared foundations
outline.gist: Shura among people who agree on nothing wastes time; separating is not division, but making enemies of those heading to the same goal is.

outline.heading: The blame is on oppressors; your duty is to convey
outline.gist: Deal well with those who differ unless they oppress. If they turn away, you were not sent as their keeper; our job is raising awareness, not their acceptance.

outline.heading: Daughters, sons, or none
outline.gist: Allah gives some daughters, some sons, some both and some none; accept that this is how He made things and work around differences.

outline.heading: A spirit by Our command; a light to guide
outline.gist: The Quran is revealed as a spirit and light by which Allah guides whom He wills to the straight path.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Difference among people is Allah's design; disputes are referred to Him.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: Difference is natural but division, meaning enmity and refusal to work together, is forbidden.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Shura among people who share foundations; separate teams toward one goal are fine.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Our job is to convey and raise awareness, not to control acceptance.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Believers avoid major sins and forgive when angry.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Believers do not stay silent when wronged; blame lies with oppressors.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Affection due to kinship, extended to all children of Adam and to the Prophet's family.

maxims: Difference and division are two different things
Difference is the norm of life
Division is only when we become enemies
Your job is only to convey
