takeaways: Surround yourself with like-minded people and consult them
Treat those who differ from you with respect and fairness
Work separately from others if needed, but never as enemies
Convey the message and leave acceptance to Allah
Stand up against oppression rather than staying silent

43:5.ar: أَفَنَضۡرِبُ عَنكُمُ ٱلذِّكۡرَ صَفۡحًا أَن كُنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا مُّسۡرِفِينَ
43:5.en: Shall We utterly ignore you because ye are a wanton folk

43:6.ar: وَكَمۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن نَّبِيࣲّ فِي ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
43:6.en: How many a prophet did We send among the men of old

43:7.ar: وَمَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن نَّبِيٍّ إِلَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
43:7.en: And never came there unto them a prophet but they used to mock him

43:8.ar: فَأَهۡلَكۡنَآ أَشَدَّ مِنۡهُم بَطۡشࣰ ا وَمَضَىٰ مَثَلُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
43:8.en: Then We destroyed men mightier than these in prowess; and the example of the men of old hath gone (before them)

43:9.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُم مَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
43:9.en: And if thou (Muhammad) ask them: Who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely answer: The Mighty, the Knower created them

43:10.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَهۡدࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا سُبُلࣰ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
43:10.en: Who made the earth a resting-place for you, and placed roads for you therein, that haply ye may find your way

43:11.ar: وَٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءَۢ بِقَدَرࣲ فَأَنشَرۡنَا بِهِۦ بَلۡدَةࣰ مَّيۡتࣰ اۚ كَذَٰلِكَ تُخۡرَجُونَ
43:11.en: And Who sendeth down water from the sky in (due) measure, and We revive a dead land therewith. Even so will ye be brought forth

43:12.ar: وَٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡأَزۡوَٰجَ كُلَّهَا وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡفُلۡكِ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ مَا تَرۡكَبُونَ
43:12.en: He Who created all the pairs, and appointed for you ships and cattle whereupon ye ride

43:13.ar: لِتَسۡتَوُۥاْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِۦ ثُمَّ تَذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ رَبِّكُمۡ إِذَا ٱسۡتَوَيۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَتَقُولُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُۥ مُقۡرِنِينَ
43:13.en: That ye may mount upon their backs, and may remember your Lord's favour when ye mount thereon, and may say: Glorified be He Who hath subdued these unto us, and we were not capable (of subduing them)

43:14.en: And lo! unto our Lord we surely are returning

43:15.ar: وَجَعَلُواْ لَهُۥ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ جُزۡءًاۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ لَكَفُورࣱ مُّبِينٌ
43:15.en: And they allot to Him a portion of His bondmen! Lo! man is verily a mere ingrate

43:16.ar: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذَ مِمَّا يَخۡلُقُ بَنَاتࣲ وَأَصۡفَىٰكُم بِٱلۡبَنِينَ
43:16.en: Or chooseth He daughters of all that He hath created, and honoureth He you with sons

43:17.ar: وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِمَا ضَرَبَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مَثَلࣰ ا ظَلَّ وَجۡهُهُۥ مُسۡوَدࣰّ ا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ
43:17.en: And if one of them hath tidings of that which he likeneth to the Beneficent One, his countenance becometh black and he is full of inward rage

43:18.ar: أَوَمَن يُنَشَّؤُاْ فِي ٱلۡحِلۡيَةِ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلۡخِصَامِ غَيۡرُ مُبِينࣲ‏
43:18.en: (Liken they then to Allah) that which is bred up in outward show, and in dispute cannot make itself plain

43:19.ar: وَجَعَلُواْ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ عِبَٰدُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ إِنَٰثًاۚ أَشَهِدُواْ خَلۡقَهُمۡۚ سَتُكۡتَبُ شَهَٰدَتُهُمۡ وَيُسۡـَٔلُونَ
43:19.en: And they make the angels, who are the slaves of the Beneficent, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned

43:20.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ شَآءَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مَا عَبَدۡنَٰهُمۗ مَّا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِنۡ هُمۡ إِلَّا يَخۡرُصُونَ
43:20.en: And they say: If the Beneficent One had (so) willed, we should not have worshipped them. They have no knowledge whatsoever of that. They do but guess

43:21.ar: أَمۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمۡ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ فَهُم بِهِۦ مُسۡتَمۡسِكُونَ
43:21.en: Or have We given them any scripture before (this Qur'an) so that they are holding fast thereto

43:22.ar: بَلۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
43:22.en: Nay, for they say only: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footprints

43:23.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ فِي قَرۡيَةࣲ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتۡرَفُوهَآ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّقۡتَدُونَ
43:23.en: And even so We sent not a warner before thee (Muhammad) into any township but its luxurious ones said: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are following their footprints

43:24.ar: ۞قَٰلَ أَوَلَوۡ جِئۡتُكُم بِأَهۡدَىٰ مِمَّا وَجَدتُّمۡ عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَكُمۡۖ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا بِمَآ أُرۡسِلۡتُم بِهِۦ كَٰفِرُونَ
43:24.en: (And the warner) said: What! Even though I bring you better guidance than that ye found your fathers following? They answered: Lo! in what ye bring we are disbelievers

43:31.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَتَيۡنِ عَظِيمٍ
43:31.en: And they say: If only this Qur'an had been revealed to some great man of the two towns

43:32.ar: أَهُمۡ يَقۡسِمُونَ رَحۡمَتَ رَبِّكَۚ نَحۡنُ قَسَمۡنَا بَيۡنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَرَفَعۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ فَوۡقَ بَعۡضࣲ دَرَجَٰتࣲ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعۡضُهُم بَعۡضࣰ ا سُخۡرِيࣰّ اۗ وَرَحۡمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ
43:32.en: Is it they who apportion thy Lord's mercy? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of the world, and raised some of them above others in rank that some of them may take labour from others; and the mercy of thy Lord is better than (the wealth) that they amass

43:33.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ لَّجَعَلۡنَا لِمَن يَكۡفُرُ بِٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمۡ سُقُفࣰ ا مِّن فِضَّةࣲ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيۡهَا يَظۡهَرُونَ
43:33.en: And were it not that mankind would have become one community, We might well have appointed, for those who disbelieve in the Beneficent, roofs of silver for their houses and stairs (of silver) whereby to mount

43:34.ar: وَلِبُيُوتِهِمۡ أَبۡوَٰبࣰ ا وَسُرُرًا عَلَيۡهَا يَتَّكِـُٔونَ
43:34.en: And for their houses doors (of silver) and couches of silver whereon to recline

43:35.ar: وَزُخۡرُفࣰ اۚ وَإِن كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:35.en: And ornaments of gold. Yet all that would have been but a provision of the life of the world. And the Hereafter with your Lord would have been for those who keep from evil

43:36.ar: وَمَن يَعۡشُ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ نُقَيِّضۡ لَهُۥ شَيۡطَٰنࣰ ا فَهُوَ لَهُۥ قَرِينࣱ‏
43:36.en: And he whose sight is dim to the remembrance of the Beneficent, We assign unto him a devil who becometh his comrade

43:43.ar: فَٱسۡتَمۡسِكۡ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
43:43.en: So hold thou fast to that which is inspired in thee. Lo! thou art on a right path

43:51.ar: وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
43:51.en: And Pharaoh caused a proclamation to be made among his people saying: O my people! Is not mine the sovereignty of Egypt and these rivers flowing under me? Can ye not then discern

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
43:52.en: I am surely better than this fellow, who is despicable and can hardly make (his meaning) plain

43:53.ar: فَلَوۡلَآ أُلۡقِيَ عَلَيۡهِ أَسۡوِرَةࣱ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ مُقۡتَرِنِينَ
43:53.en: Why, then, have armlets of gold not been set upon him, or angels sent along with him

43:54.ar: فَٱسۡتَخَفَّ قَوۡمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
43:54.en: Thus he persuaded his people to make light (of Moses), and they obeyed him. Lo! they were a wanton folk

43:55.ar: فَلَمَّآ ءَاسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
43:55.en: So, when they angered Us, We punished them and drowned them every one

43:56.ar: فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ سَلَفࣰ ا وَمَثَلࣰ ا لِّلۡأٓخِرِينَ
43:56.en: And We made them a thing past, and an example for those after (them)

43:57.ar: ۞وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذَا قَوۡمُكَ مِنۡهُ يَصِدُّونَ
43:57.en: And when the son of Mary is quoted as an example, behold! the folk laugh out

43:67.ar: ٱلۡأَخِلَّآءُ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بَعۡضُهُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:67.en: Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty (to Allah)

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
43:81.en: Say (O Muhammad): If the Beneficent One hath a son, then, I shall be first among the worshippers. (But there is no son)

43:82.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ
43:82.en: Glorified be the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, from that which they ascribe (unto Him)

43:83.ar: فَذَرۡهُمۡ يَخُوضُواْ وَيَلۡعَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
43:83.en: So let them flounder (in their talk) and play until they meet the Day which they are promised

43:84.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَٰهࣱ وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَٰهࣱۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
43:84.en: And He it is Who in the heaven is Allah, and in the earth Allah. He is the Wise, the Knower

43:85.ar: وَتَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا وَعِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
43:85.en: And blessed be He unto Whom belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and with Whom is knowledge of the Hour, and unto Whom ye will be returned

43:86.ar: وَلَا يَمۡلِكُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةَ إِلَّا مَن شَهِدَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
43:86.en: And those unto whom they cry instead of Him possess no power of intercession, saving him who beareth witness unto the Truth knowingly

43:87.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُم مَّنۡ خَلَقَهُمۡ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُۖ فَأَنَّىٰ يُؤۡفَكُونَ
43:87.en: And if thou ask them who created them, they will surely say: Allah. How then are they turned away

43:88.ar: وَقِيلِهِۦ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
43:88.en: And he saith: O my Lord! Lo! these are a folk who believe not

43:89.ar: فَٱصۡفَحۡ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقُلۡ سَلَٰمࣱۚ فَسَوۡفَ يَعۡلَمُونَ
43:89.en: Then bear with them (O Muhammad) and say: Peace. But they will come to know

43:37.ar: وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
43:37.en: And lo! they surely turn them from the way of Allah, and yet they deem that they are rightly guided

43:38.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَنَا قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَكَ بُعۡدَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقَيۡنِ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡقَرِينُ
43:38.en: Till, when he cometh unto Us, he saith (unto his comrade): Ah, would that between me and thee there were the distance of the two horizons - an evil comrade

43:39.ar: وَلَن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ إِذ ظَّلَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ مُشۡتَرِكُونَ
43:39.en: And it profiteth you not this day, because ye did wrong, that ye will be sharers in the doom

43:40.ar: أَفَأَنتَ تُسۡمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ أَوۡ تَهۡدِي ٱلۡعُمۡيَ وَمَن كَانَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
43:40.en: Canst thou (Muhammad) make the deaf to hear, or canst thou guide the blind or him who is in error manifest

43:41.ar: فَإِمَّا نَذۡهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنۡهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ
43:41.en: And if We take thee away, We surely shall take vengeance on them

43:42.ar: أَوۡ نُرِيَنَّكَ ٱلَّذِي وَعَدۡنَٰهُمۡ فَإِنَّا عَلَيۡهِم مُّقۡتَدِرُونَ

r4vipnn510E.title: Surat Az-Zukhruf Summary
r4vipnn510E.one_line: Az-Zukhruf warns against materialist logic that judges God, prophets and people, especially women, by wealth and glitter.
r4vipnn510E.summary: Delivered partly in English and partly in Arabic, this summary places Az-Zukhruf among the Hawamim, which give advice and warnings for those calling to Allah. Its warning is against the logic of zukhruf, glittering ornament: a materialist mindset that values only what shines and can be measured. Extravagance as a lifestyle does not exempt anyone from the reminder. Materialism makes faith in an unseen God hard, so the surah teaches a prayer when mounting a ship or animal, a reminder that creation has a non-material side. The same logic made pre-Islamic Arabs despise daughters, whose material return seemed lower. He argues that today's consumer culture still values women by appearance, and that the appearance of freedom in this country is false. Hijab, with men's lowered gaze, is meant to make society judge a woman by her character and knowledge. Further examples: the wealthy who see no need to change, Quraysh asking why the Quran was not sent to a rich notable, Pharaoh boasting of his rivers against Musa's halting speech, and Isa as the model of detachment. Allah would have given disbelievers silver roofs were it not for people all turning to disbelief. He urges holding fast to revelation and sound reason, which Islam never separates.

outline.heading: Opening

outline.heading: Extravagance, and the Creator they cannot see
outline.gist: Allah will not withhold the reminder from an extravagant people; they admit Allah created all, yet need something tangible to worship. The prayer on mounting ships and animals.

outline.heading: More than material: the prayer when travelling
outline.gist: The vehicles that carry us are a reminder that daily life has a dimension beyond materialism.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Hawamim: advice and warnings for callers
outline.gist: Ghafir: call while entrusting your affairs to Allah. Fussilat: action calls more powerfully than words. Ash-Shura: people differ; surround yourself with the like-minded, consult and treat others well.

outline.heading: Not everything that glitters is gold
outline.gist: Zukhruf is whatever catches the eye though it may be worthless or harmful; materialist logic corrupts thinking and life.

outline.heading: Extravagance as a way of life
outline.gist: Excess in money, time, emotion and play is condemned; being extravagant does not exempt anyone from the reminder.

outline.heading: Why materialism makes faith hard
outline.gist: Because Allah cannot be seen, heard or touched, materialists look for something else to worship. He made mounts to carry our loads.

outline.heading: Daughters ascribed to Allah
outline.gist: They assign daughters to Allah while their own faces darken at news of a girl, and call the angels female.

outline.heading: Valuing genders by material worth, then and now
outline.gist: The same broken logic made genders unequal; consumer culture still values women by appearance over what they have to say.

outline.heading: Hijab: judge her by her character
outline.gist: Concealment forces people to listen to a woman and judge her by character; Islam came to liberate women, while today's pressure to look a certain way is unfair.

outline.heading: 'Had Ar-Rahman willed, we would not have worshipped them'
outline.gist: The affluent of every town rejected warners and clung to their forefathers' way.

outline.heading: Measuring people by money
outline.gist: Arabs valued sons who fought and earned over daughters; a hateful logic for which they will be questioned.

outline.heading: The false appearance of freedom
outline.gist: Do not be fooled here: women are still valued materially and pressured in dress and manner. Modesty for men and hijab for women free a woman from being a commodity judged by appearance.

outline.heading: The wealthy feel no need for change
outline.gist: Their claim that Allah could force them otherwise is crooked logic; those with money and comfort resist every warner.

outline.heading: Why not a great man of the two towns?
outline.gist: Quraysh wanted the Quran sent to a rich notable. Do they apportion your Lord's mercy? Allah divided livelihoods so people serve one another.

outline.heading: Roofs of silver for disbelievers
outline.gist: Silver roofs, stairways, doors and couches are only the enjoyment of this life; the Hereafter is for the God-conscious.

outline.heading: The Prophet, greatest of creation, judged poor
outline.gist: Materialist logic could not see that Muhammad, lacking wealth, is the best of creation and master of humanity on the Day.

outline.heading: Were it not that all would disbelieve
outline.gist: Allah would give disbelievers all the glitter they want, but that would keep everyone in disbelief, so wealth is spread unevenly to make people reflect.

outline.heading: A materialist environment harming our children
outline.gist: We are losing our way as Muslims; is making money all we do?

outline.heading: Blind to the remembrance; hold fast to revelation
outline.gist: Materialism blinds; money has value only for sufficiency and for spending on those without. Hold fast to what was revealed.

outline.heading: Pharaoh: is not Egypt mine?
outline.gist: Pharaoh compared his kingdom and rivers to Musa's halting speech; he made fools of his people and they obeyed, by their own choice.

outline.heading: Don't be dazzled by the glitter
outline.gist: Even children would reject Pharaoh's logic, yet many of us are taken in by zukhruf.

outline.heading: Isa: the model of detachment
outline.gist: The best-known name on earth left the world owning nothing.

outline.heading: Friends become enemies, except the God-conscious
outline.gist: Friendships built on interest turn to enmity on the Day; only those for Allah's sake last.

outline.heading: If Ar-Rahman had a son, I would be first to worship
outline.gist: Sound reasoning, not materialist logic, settles the question; if they refuse, turn away and say peace.

outline.heading: A religion built on reason
outline.gist: Islam does not set revelation against reason; it is built on sound thinking.

hRaWafeTOIw.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 4: Efficiency and Effectiveness
hRaWafeTOIw.one_line: Doing the right thing and doing it right together make ihsan; Muslims need decisiveness, work ethic, right people in right roles, teamwork and planning.
hRaWafeTOIw.summary: The sheikh starts from a familiar frustration: large Muslim communities and long meetings that achieve little. He defines effectiveness as doing the right thing and efficiency as doing things right; together they are ihsan, excellence, which Allah loves and rewards and which the Prophet required even when slaughtering an animal. He then diagnoses why Muslims lack both. First is a lack of decisiveness and full commitment: the Quran repeatedly tells the Prophet not to be distracted, the believers at the Confederates were not shaken by numbers, and Musa was told to take the tablets with strength. The trench, divided among sixty teams and finished early despite hunger, shows the Prophet's planning. Second is weak work ethic, which is an ethical matter tied to halal income and keeping agreements, as seen in the Prophet's honest trading and his sending a man back to repeat a careless prayer. Third is placing unqualified people in authority. Fourth is the absence of teamwork: cooperate on what you agree on and excuse each other on the rest. He also urges people simply to do their own role, citing the hadith of planting a sapling as the Hour comes. His action plan is to find where you fit, plan as an act of worship, and use an urgent-important matrix to protect long-term goals.

sP8a-BmHaF8.title: Towards a Modern Awakening: Q&A Session
sP8a-BmHaF8.one_line: Q&A after the Modern Awakening series: basic Islamic knowledge, formal education, mentorship, youth power, institutional vision, culture versus deen, and building values.
sP8a-BmHaF8.summary: Answering viewer questions after his series, the sheikh lays out what a Muslim community in London needs to wake up. On knowledge, he refuses to set a minimum amount but asks everyone to study one simple text in each discipline (creed, fiqh of one school, Quran sciences) and to pair knowledge with a healthy, open outlook, since information without perspective can make people narrower. He notes that structured, certified Islamic education does not exist in the city and could be built on the old ijazah model if enough people commit. Mentorship should be organised by the community, and the key mentors are people in their twenties, as he was when he taught Quran to village children at fifteen. He tells university students they are the most powerful demographic and that institutions will respond once youth demand programs and vision. Leadership's real gap is a shared, practical vision; the cure for weak institutions is public involvement. He argues Islam is the stronger idea and need not fear rational questions, but culture has been allowed to overrule the deen, which drives logical youth away. Values are built through deep reflection (tafakkur) and by revisiting one's own behaviour after each encounter. He closes by listing missing services and asking the public to say what it needs.

outline.heading: What a local program would need
outline.gist: Funding, trained teachers, a curriculum and even high school credits in Arabic or Islamic history.

outline.heading: Mentorship must be organised by the community
outline.gist: The Muslim Fellowship Network idea never launched; matching mentors and youth is leadership's job, but meanwhile youth should ask busy, accomplished people to mentor them.

outline.heading: Mentors for young sisters and help for parents
outline.gist: The community has many practising women who can mentor girls, and parents should actively find mentors for their teenagers in a fast-changing world.

outline.heading: Youth-driven academic programs
outline.gist: Institutions began with basic Quran classes; attractive academic programs must be designed by youth, with scholars offering content and supervision.

outline.heading: Youth are the most powerful demographic
outline.gist: University students have the passion, time and numbers to force any institution to change; if they unite and demand programs, masajid must respond.

outline.heading: Interlude
Investing in online outreach
outline.gist: The London community never invested in social media; the pandemic showed that teaching must be offered online while keeping interaction alive.

outline.heading: Interlude
Leadership's missing piece is vision
outline.gist: Institutional leaders lack a shared, practical five-year vision for every domain and must keep their ears to the ground.

outline.heading: Fix where you live: get involved
outline.gist: Care for the ummah starts locally; London's institutions are not at war, and the real problem is public disinterest, so people should take memberships and demand cooperation.

outline.heading: Networking starts with institutions
outline.gist: Networking is outside his expertise, but it should begin with leaders meeting each other; knowing people reduces assumptions and builds support.

outline.heading: Islam is the stronger idea and fears no debate
outline.gist: Because revelation is truth, Muslims should explain it rationally and openly; hiding knowledge out of fear is a grave wrong.

outline.heading: When culture rules the deen
outline.gist: Culture is given the last word over religion; parents present cultural rules as Islam, logical youth see the flaws and lose faith, so parents must learn the deen and choose their battles.

outline.heading: Teaching Quran at fifteen in his Syrian village
outline.gist: He began teaching four children at home, grew to hundreds in the masjid, while men in their twenties mentored him: mentors must be close in age.

outline.heading: People in their twenties as the key mentors
outline.gist: Twenty-somethings are at their peak and can mentor the younger generation; scholars will supply the knowledge they lack.

outline.heading: Building values through deep reflection (tafakkur)
outline.gist: Values form from beliefs reinforced by thought and community; tafakkur is an underrated act of worship practised by the Prophet and all scholars.

outline.heading: Revisit your behaviour after each encounter
outline.gist: Instead of forgetting embarrassing moments, trace back which value produced the behaviour and work on it.

outline.heading: Ideas are many, champions are few
outline.gist: Contact leaders and youth board members with suggestions, but what is lacking is people who carry an idea to completion, even outside institutions.

outline.heading: Services the community lacks
outline.gist: Formal and structured Islamic education, mental health support and better narratives, immigrant integration, tutoring and career guidance.

outline.heading: The public should state its needs
outline.gist: Leaders should not guess; surveys and public involvement should define the services institutions provide.

outline.heading: Outro

MAr5FpehDjU.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 2: Intellect and Thought
MAr5FpehDjU.one_line: The ummah's crisis is a crisis of thought; Muslims need evidence-based smart faith and must overcome superstition, partisanship, closed-mindedness and blind tradition.
MAr5FpehDjU.summary: The sheikh argues that a nation is measured by its ideas, not its possessions, and that the Muslim struggle today is intellectual rather than financial, military or political. The first revealed word, iqra, calls for reading life, history and nature, and the Quran repeatedly ends its signs by asking people to think. The Prophet's real legacy was a superior idea, so Muslims should follow how he thought before how he dressed. He contrasts Ibrahim breaking idols with the Prophet changing the idol mindset so the idols fell on their own. Today Islamic narratives fail the youth, Jumuah is wasted as a channel of learning, and many misunderstand Islam's breadth, its constants and variables, and its priorities. Islam rests on evidence, so it cannot conflict with science, and the Quran condemns ignorance above all. Muslims must relearn how to disagree respectfully and should defeat extremism by out-arguing it. He names four obstacles: superstition, blind partisanship to schools or sheikhs, closed-mindedness toward new ideas, and sanctifying inherited culture. His action plan is for each person to take responsibility for learning Islam properly, question what they are taught until it makes sense, and treat ignorance as the main enemy.

outline.heading: A nation is valued by its thoughts

outline.gist: The first revealed word means reading life, history and nature, and the first verses are full of knowledge.

outline.gist: Spending the night drawing lessons from the hadith of the child whose bird died was judged better than a night of prayer.

outline.heading: The Prophet's legacy was an idea
outline.gist: Muslims conquered through a superior idea, so follow how the Prophet thought about people, worship, peace and war.

outline.heading: Breaking idols vs breaking the idol mindset
outline.gist: Ibrahim's people rebuilt their idols, but the Prophet changed minds so the idols of Makkah fell at the touch of his stick.

outline.heading: Narratives that fail our youth; Jumuah as a teaching system
outline.gist: Islamic narratives do not answer young people's questions, and the weekly Jumuah meant to educate millions has been wasted.

outline.heading: Misunderstanding Islam's breadth
outline.gist: Islam as a universal, moderate wide river with fixed fundamentals, room for difference, and commands of different rank.

outline.heading: A religion of evidence and proof (43:81)
outline.gist: The Quran challenges opponents to bring proof, showing Islam works by argument.

outline.heading: Islam and science cannot contradict
outline.gist: Revelation and creation share one Source; disagree with a theory on scientific grounds, not because you think Islam forces you to.

outline.heading: Smart faith
outline.gist: We have smart everything except faith; belief should rest on evidence, revelation and logic.

outline.heading: The Quran's harshest judgement is on ignorance
outline.gist: The worst creatures are those who do not reason, and religion mixed with ignorance has produced decades of harm.

outline.heading: Learning to disagree again
outline.gist: Great scholars differed on serious issues yet respected each other; questions deserve dialogue, not one-word answers.

outline.heading: The real struggle is one of thought
outline.gist: Extremism is defeated by proving its ideas wrong, and the Prophet never refused a debate because he had the stronger idea.

outline.heading: Obstacle: superstition
outline.gist: Superstition fills Muslim homes, embarrasses us and harms youth and people with mental illness.

outline.heading: Obstacle: blind partisanship
outline.gist: Clinging blindly to a school of thought or sheikh blocks solutions; even Islam is held through evidence, not partisanship.

outline.heading: Obstacle: closed-mindedness
outline.gist: New ideas should be met with evidence, not fear; the Prophet adopted Salman's Persian idea of the trench.

outline.heading: Obstacle: sanctifying tradition and culture
outline.gist: Putting inherited custom above evidence is what the Quran condemns in those who followed their forefathers; thoughts dictate behaviour.

outline.heading: This Ramadan as a chance for radical change
outline.gist: Time at home is an opportunity from Allah to reconsider our positions.

outline.heading: Action plan: learn Islam and question everything
outline.gist: Teachers who are not questioned drift; keep asking until the answer makes sense.

outline.heading: Never asked to follow blindly
outline.gist: The Prophet taught the companions to ask and object, and we must learn to debate and converse.

outline.heading: How the companions were transformed
outline.gist: Compare a companion's life before and after Islam to see what learning to think did to him.

outline.heading: Ignorance is the number one enemy
outline.gist: Overcoming it gives a narrative our children can be proud of and real answers to hard questions.

cp61FuJuIGk.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 7: Service Mindset
cp61FuJuIGk.one_line: We were created as servants: serving Allah means serving His creation, without ego or agenda, and individuals and institutions must become service-oriented.
cp61FuJuIGk.summary: In the series finale the sheikh presents a service mindset as the thread tying together leadership, intellect, mentorship, values, sincerity and effectiveness. He reads the verse on creation for worship through the root meaning of servanthood, a humble, levelled road, and stewardship as responsibility to serve the earth. Since Allah needs nothing from us, serving Him means serving His creation. He gathers Quranic and prophetic texts: the foam that vanishes while what benefits people remains, the denier who repels the orphan, preferring others while in need, easing hardships, the most beloved people being the most beneficial, and the Prophet's character before prophethood as Khadijah described it. A servant has no agenda and no ego; those who do not serve either try to control people or complain. He lists six components of service: sincerity, humility, trust in Allah, trust in people, striving and sacrifice. Individuals who think this way would stop pushing for spots, and institutions should see people as needs to meet, not donors, since masjids belong to Allah. The Prophet listened to people for hours, calmed a man who choked him, and corrected a Bedouin who urinated in the masjid gently. He laments roughness learned under dictatorships and asks for a personal shift toward finding a way to serve.

outline.heading: Service as the thread of the whole series
outline.gist: Every earlier episode was a build-up to the service mindset.

outline.heading: Leadership and followship exist for service
outline.gist: Leaders and followers must be oriented toward serving people or nothing works.

outline.heading: Thought, mentorship and networking as service
outline.gist: Islamic thought should make ideas simple for people; mentorship is the most intimate form of service.

outline.heading: Service: the missing value; the ego that wants to be served
outline.gist: Purification trains the self, which wants to be served, to serve instead.

outline.heading: The right thing to do is to serve
outline.gist: Effectiveness means discovering which services are needed, efficiency means delivering them well.

outline.heading: Created for servanthood (51:56)
outline.gist: 'Abd means servant and 'ibadah comes from a levelled, humble road; we exist to serve.

outline.heading: Stewardship as responsibility to serve
outline.gist: The khalifah is responsible for the earth and those on it, a foundation missing from how we view Islam.

outline.heading: Serving Allah means serving His creation
outline.gist: Nothing we do benefits Allah, so we serve Him by serving those He created.

outline.heading: You alone we serve (1:5)
outline.gist: From the opening of the Quran, worship is framed as service.

outline.heading: Foam passes, what benefits people remains (13:17)
outline.gist: Truth is what sinks in and benefits people; falsehood floats and vanishes.

outline.heading: Quran on feeding the needy and preferring others
outline.gist: The denier repels the orphan, the people of Hell did not feed the poor, the Ansar preferred others, and the steep path is feeding the hungry when hungry.

outline.heading: Ease a hardship and Allah eases yours
outline.gist: Allah helps a servant as long as he helps his brother.

outline.heading: The most beloved to Allah are the most beneficial
outline.gist: The most beloved deeds bring joy to a Muslim, remove hunger or pay off debt.

outline.heading: Walking with a brother in need
outline.gist: Better than a month of i'tikaf in the Prophet's masjid, and it steadies your feet on Judgement Day.

outline.heading: Caring for orphans and widows
outline.gist: The orphan's guardian is with the Prophet in Jannah; caring for widows equals fighting in Allah's path or constant fasting and prayer.

outline.heading: Khadijah describes the Prophet's character
outline.gist: Before prophethood he kept ties, supported the weak, helped earners and stood by those in calamity.

outline.heading: Servants have no agenda and no ego
outline.gist: A servant cares only for the satisfaction of the One served and eats last.

outline.heading: Serve, control or complain
outline.gist: We are not here to control people's thoughts or behaviour on Allah's behalf but to serve them.

outline.heading: The complainers
outline.gist: Those with a million ideas and no effort; a paradigm shift is needed now.

outline.heading: Component of service: sincerity
outline.gist: Service needs a high level of sincerity, hence the episode on intention.

outline.heading: Component of service: humility
outline.gist: We are servants by creation; Allah alone is Supreme, and if this bothers you revise your values.

outline.heading: Component of service: trust in Allah
outline.gist: Serve Him and trust that He will be satisfied and take care of you.

outline.heading: Component of service: trust in people
outline.gist: Controllers distrust the public; serve people well and they will choose rightly.

outline.heading: Component of service: striving
outline.gist: Service is hard, always more to do, a lifelong mujahadah.

outline.heading: Component of service: sacrifice
outline.gist: Service costs ego, wealth, time and life.

outline.heading: Service-oriented individuals
outline.gist: Servants would not fight over spots or push; they let others go first and take care of themselves last.

outline.heading: Serve even if others don't
outline.gist: Perfect your own servanthood and leave others to their accountability.

outline.heading: Service-oriented institutions
outline.gist: See visitors as people with needs, not donors or popularity; masjids belong to Allah, not boards.

outline.heading: Mutual service dissolves our problems
outline.gist: If everyone tried to serve each other, conflicts would disappear.

outline.heading: The Prophet served day and night
outline.gist: He would stand for an hour listening to an old woman's problems; sometimes giving an ear is the service.

outline.heading: Give the Prophet space (33:53)
outline.gist: Revelation told companions not to linger after meals because he was too shy to ask them to leave.

outline.heading: The man who twisted his collar and the runaway camel
outline.gist: He gave the man until he was pleased, then explained that gentleness brought him back like a frightened camel coaxed with grass.

outline.heading: Paying with ego: the Bedouin in the masjid
outline.gist: He let the man finish urinating, then taught him gently, winning him over.

outline.heading: Roughness learned under dictatorships
outline.gist: Oppression made societies harsh and selfish, and some of that has rubbed off on Muslims.

outline.heading: Serving kindly for money but not for Allah?
outline.gist: Public service staff greet people warmly because they are paid; can money be worth more to us than Allah's reward?

outline.heading: Action plan: a paradigm shift to service
outline.gist: Find something you are good at and enjoy, serve people through it, and bring service-oriented people into institutions.

outline.heading: Interlude
A modern awakening fit for our reality
outline.gist: It will carry the same values as the early Muslims but look different, wherever Muslims live.

N3GRPR-6rEA.speaker: adnan
N3GRPR-6rEA.speaker_note: sixth episode of his own series; speaks of how he was raised and taught Islam
N3GRPR-6rEA.title: Towards a Modern Awakening, Ep. 6: Intentions and Spirituality
N3GRPR-6rEA.one_line: Sincerity and purification of the soul are the heart of Islam; the ummah's real problem is ego, and every Muslim needs a path of tazkiyah.
N3GRPR-6rEA.summary: The sheikh treats intention and purification of the soul as the core of the faith. Hadith collections open with the hadith on intentions, and Surat al-Ikhlas names sincerity as the natural fruit of pure monotheism. He tells of Sufyan pausing to correct his intention before a funeral, and Ali sparing an enemy who spat at him so he would not fight for himself. Allah rejects any deed shared with a partner and cares more about motive than outcome. Following the best of revelation means choosing, in each moment, the most sincere command rather than the most convenient, such as quoting rulings at a spouse or attacking someone you already dislike. Imperfect intention is never a reason to stop a good deed. The ummah's deepest problem is ego. Purification is one of the four purposes for which prophets were sent and the subject of eleven consecutive oaths in Surat ash-Shams, yet it goes unmentioned in many Muslim homes. Pharaoh's ruin was arrogance, and knowledge without a grown heart misleads. He describes four major diseases of the heart, vanity, arrogance, showing off and envy, with remedies of praise, seeing one's own faults, exalting Allah and team spirit, plus love of the Prophet. He urges finding a teacher of tazkiyah, keeping daily remembrance and Quran, and reading classical works on the heart.

outline.heading: Why intention deserves its own treatment
outline.gist: He would rather say purification than spirituality; intention is singled out because the Prophet and the scholars treated it that way.

outline.heading: Actions are by intentions
outline.gist: Hadith books open with this narration, and sincerity is the thing to revisit throughout life.

outline.heading: Surat al-Ikhlas: sincerity as fruit of tawhid
outline.gist: The only surah whose name is absent from its text; believing in the One God produces sincere worship.

outline.heading: Sufyan pauses to correct his intention
outline.gist: Before a funeral he sat a moment to make sure his intention was right, and asked his students why they did not.

outline.heading: Ali and the enemy who spat
outline.gist: Ali walked away rather than strike in personal anger, since he fought only for Allah.

outline.heading: Allah needs no partner in a deed
outline.gist: Deeds shared with others are left to those partners; Allah weighs the motive above the outcome.

outline.heading: Commanded to worship with sincerity (39:11)
outline.gist: Everything in the religion is to be done purely for Allah.

outline.heading: Follow the best of it (7:145, 39:18, 39:55)
outline.gist: Of many applicable rulings, choose the one that best serves the religion and pleases Allah most in your situation.

outline.heading: Convenient vs sincere
outline.gist: Lecturing children, quoting hadith at a spouse, or publicly correcting someone you dislike may be convenient but not sincere.

outline.heading: Never stop a deed for imperfect intention
outline.gist: Keep doing good while caring about your intention.

outline.heading: The ummah's real problem is ego
outline.gist: Our masjids can fit our bodies but the universe cannot fit our egos; most disputes trace back to ego.

outline.heading: Purification is why prophets were sent (3:164)
outline.gist: Of the four prophetic purposes, purifying hearts comes second, yet it is barely mentioned in Muslim homes.

outline.heading: Imam Malik sent to learn manners
outline.gist: His mother sent him to learn his teacher's conduct before his knowledge, and he became known for reverence.

outline.heading: Eleven oaths for one result (91:1-10)
outline.gist: Allah swears by sun, moon, day, night, sky, earth and soul that whoever purifies the soul succeeds.

outline.heading: Desires aligned with revelation
outline.gist: No one fully believes until his desires follow what the Prophet brought; the self leads to Jannah or Hell.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's root problem was arrogance (79:18-19)
outline.gist: Musa offered to help him purify himself and find his Lord; he refused.

outline.heading: Restraining desires vs worshipping them (79:40-41, 45:23)
outline.gist: Taking one's desire as a god can mislead even someone full of knowledge.

outline.heading: Big brain, small heart
outline.gist: Knowledge must grow alongside the heart; his own upbringing centred on purification.

outline.heading: We cannot know if a deed is accepted
outline.gist: Sincerity and fewer diseases of the heart raise the likelihood of acceptance, hence asking Allah to accept after prayer.

outline.heading: Accepted deeds bring light to the heart
outline.gist: Some get nothing from fasting but hunger and from night prayer but fatigue.

outline.heading: The diseases of the heart
outline.gist: Scholars count 25 to 30; four major ones are born in everyone to different degrees and grow unless removed.

outline.heading: Vanity vs confidence: the cure of praise
outline.gist: Shaytan pushes toward vanity or low self-esteem; praising Allah moves the spotlight from you to Him.

outline.heading: Arrogance vs humility: the cure of seeking forgiveness

44:2.en: By the Scripture that maketh plain

44:3.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ فِي لَيۡلَةࣲ مُّبَٰرَكَةٍۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ
44:3.en: Lo! We revealed it on a blessed night - Lo! We are ever warning

44:4.en: Whereon every wise command is made clear

44:5.ar: أَمۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡ عِندِنَآۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُرۡسِلِينَ
44:5.en: As a command from Our presence - Lo! We are ever sending

44:6.ar: رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
44:6.en: A mercy from thy Lord. Lo! He, even He is the Hearer, the Knower

44:7.ar: رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
44:7.en: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye would be sure

44:8.ar: لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۖ رَبُّكُمۡ وَرَبُّ ءَابَآئِكُمُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
44:8.en: There is no Allah save Him. He quickeneth and giveth death; your Lord and Lord of your forefathers

44:9.en: Nay, but they play in doubt

44:10.ar: فَٱرۡتَقِبۡ يَوۡمَ تَأۡتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
44:10.en: But watch thou (O Muhammad) for the day when the sky will produce visible smoke

44:11.en: That will envelop the people. This will be a painful torment

44:12.ar: رَّبَّنَا ٱكۡشِفۡ عَنَّا ٱلۡعَذَابَ إِنَّا مُؤۡمِنُونَ
44:12.en: (Then they will say): Our Lord relieve us of the torment. Lo! we are believers

44:13.ar: أَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ وَقَدۡ جَآءَهُمۡ رَسُولࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
44:13.en: How can there be remembrance for them, when a messenger making plain (the Truth) had already come unto them

44:14.ar: ثُمَّ تَوَلَّوۡاْ عَنۡهُ وَقَالُواْ مُعَلَّمࣱ مَّجۡنُونٌ
44:14.en: And they had turned away from him and said: One taught (by others), a madman

44:15.ar: إِنَّا كَاشِفُواْ ٱلۡعَذَابِ قَلِيلًاۚ إِنَّكُمۡ عَآئِدُونَ
44:15.en: Lo! We withdraw the torment a little. Lo! ye return (to disbelief)

44:16.ar: يَوۡمَ نَبۡطِشُ ٱلۡبَطۡشَةَ ٱلۡكُبۡرَىٰٓ إِنَّا مُنتَقِمُونَ
44:16.en: On the day when We shall seize them with the greater seizure, (then) in truth We shall punish

44:17.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمَ فِرۡعَوۡنَ وَجَآءَهُمۡ رَسُولࣱ كَرِيمٌ
44:17.en: And verily We tried before them Pharaoh's folk, when there came unto them a noble messenger

44:18.ar: أَنۡ أَدُّوٓاْ إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّي لَكُمۡ رَسُولٌ أَمِينࣱ‏
44:18.en: Saying: Give up to me the slaves of Allah. Lo! I am a faithful messenger unto you

44:19.ar: وَأَن لَّا تَعۡلُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّيٓ ءَاتِيكُم بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
44:19.en: And saying: Be not proud against Allah. Lo! I bring you a clear warrant

44:20.ar: وَإِنِّي عُذۡتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمۡ أَن تَرۡجُمُونِ
44:20.en: And lo! I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest ye stone me to death

44:21.en: And if ye put no faith in me, then let me go

44:22.ar: فَدَعَا رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنَّ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمࣱ مُّجۡرِمُونَ
44:22.en: And he cried unto his Lord, (saying): These are guilty folk

44:23.en: Then (his Lord commanded): Take away My slaves by night. Lo! ye will be followed

44:24.ar: وَٱتۡرُكِ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ رَهۡوًاۖ إِنَّهُمۡ جُندࣱ مُّغۡرَقُونَ
44:24.en: And leave the sea behind at rest, for lo! they are a drowned host

44:25.en: How many were the gardens and the watersprings that they left behind

44:26.en: And the cornlands and the goodly sites

44:27.en: And pleasant things wherein they took delight

44:28.en: Even so (it was), and We made it an inheritance for other folk

44:29.ar: فَمَا بَكَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنظَرِينَ
44:29.en: And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved

44:30.ar: وَلَقَدۡ نَجَّيۡنَا بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡمُهِينِ
44:30.en: And We delivered the Children of Israel from the shameful doom

44:31.ar: مِن فِرۡعَوۡنَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ عَالِيࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ
44:31.en: (We delivered them) from Pharaoh. Lo! he was a tyrant of the wanton ones

44:32.ar: وَلَقَدِ ٱخۡتَرۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
44:32.en: And We chose them, purposely, above (all) creatures

44:33.ar: وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلَٰٓؤࣱ اْ مُّبِينٌ
44:33.en: And We gave them portents wherein was a clear trial

44:35.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا مَوۡتَتُنَا ٱلۡأُولَىٰ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُنشَرِينَ
44:35.en: There is naught but our first death, and we shall not be raised again

44:36.en: Bring back our fathers, if ye speak the truth

44:37.ar: أَهُمۡ خَيۡرٌ أَمۡ قَوۡمُ تُبَّعࣲ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَٰهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ مُجۡرِمِينَ
44:37.en: Are they better, or the folk of Tubb'a and those before them? We destroyed them, for surely they were guilty

44:38.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا لَٰعِبِينَ
44:38.en: And We created not the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in play

44:39.ar: مَا خَلَقۡنَٰهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
44:39.en: We created them not save with truth; but most of them know not

44:40.en: Assuredly the Day of Decision is the term for all of them

44:41.ar: يَوۡمَ لَا يُغۡنِي مَوۡلًى عَن مَّوۡلࣰ ى شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
44:41.en: A day when friend can in naught avail friend, nor can they be helped

44:42.ar: إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
44:42.en: Save him on whom Allah hath mercy. Lo! He is the Mighty, the Merciful

44:45.en: Like molten brass, it seetheth in their bellies

44:46.en: As the seething of boiling water

44:47.en: (And it will be said): Take him and drag him to the midst of hell

44:48.ar: ثُمَّ صُبُّواْ فَوۡقَ رَأۡسِهِۦ مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱلۡحَمِيمِ
44:48.en: Then pour upon his head the torment of boiling water

44:49.en: (Saying): Taste! Lo! thou wast forsooth the mighty, the noble

44:50.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا مَا كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَمۡتَرُونَ
44:50.en: Lo! this is that whereof ye used to doubt

44:51.en: Lo! those who kept their duty will be in a place secured

44:53.en: Attired in silk and silk embroidery, facing one another

44:54.en: Even so (it will be). And We shall wed them unto fair ones with wide, lovely eyes

44:55.en: They call therein for every fruit in safety

44:56.ar: لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِلَّا ٱلۡمَوۡتَةَ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَوَقَىٰهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
44:56.en: They taste not death therein, save the first death. And He hath saved them from the doom of hell

44:57.ar: فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّكَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
44:57.en: A bounty from thy Lord. That is the supreme triumph

44:58.en: And We have made (this Scripture) easy in thy language only that they may heed

44:59.en: Wait then (O Muhammad). Lo! they (too) are waiting

2tiX_U5pw2s.title: Surat Ad-Dukhan Summary
2tiX_U5pw2s.one_line: Ad-Dukhan warns believers against taking the deen lightly: doubt breeds play, smoke signals fire, and creation was not made in jest.
2tiX_U5pw2s.summary: He explains the purpose of the surah summaries: seeing each surah as a unit with a goal, and seeing how it fits the cluster around it, so that reading it has a compass. Ad-Dukhan sits in the eighth cluster, the seven Ha-Mim surahs, which give advice and warnings for those who serve the deen. The first three gave advice on dawah; the last three give warnings, and Ad-Dukhan is the second warning: beware of taking this matter lightly, of indifference, play and a false sense of security. The surah opens with the Quran sent down on a blessed night in which every wise matter is decreed, and says this is clear to those with certainty. People instead sit in doubt and play. Smoke, usually the prop of illusion, is in fact the warning of a fire, and fire is never taken lightly. Pharaoh is the model of self-deception through wealth and power; when he and his people drowned, heaven and earth did not weep for them, a reminder that none of us is the centre of the universe and we matter only if Allah values us. Allah did not create the heavens and earth in play. The surah closes with the Day of Sorting, the tree of zaqqum and the command to wait and watch. He asks listeners to stop treating the deen, status and wealth as a game.

outline.heading: Opening
Why summarise surahs: each surah is a unit with a goal
outline.gist: The Quran is organised into clusters with a rhythm; seeing a surah from afar gives you a compass when you read it.

outline.heading: The eighth cluster: the seven Ha-Mim surahs
outline.gist: They give advice and warnings to those who serve the deen before the Quran moves into the details of that service.

outline.heading: The first three Ha-Mims: advice on dawah
outline.gist: Take the message to those who resist, let actions speak louder than words, and hold firmly to Allah as the reference and to shura.

outline.heading: The warnings, and where Ad-Dukhan sits
outline.gist: The second three warn against materialism and taking things lightly; Ad-Dukhan is a short Makki surah long loved by elders, though no authentic hadith singles it out.

outline.heading: The theme: do not take serving Allah lightly
outline.gist: Comfort and overconfidence about our safety and futures make us inattentive to something that deserves full seriousness.

outline.heading: A blessed night where every wise matter is decreed
outline.gist: The Quran's descent and its becoming a law for mankind is a serious, clear decree, understood by those who have certainty.

outline.heading: Doubt leads people to play
outline.gist: Instead of taking time to understand, people let uncertainty make them indifferent, so they play.

outline.heading: Smoke: not illusion but a warning of fire
outline.gist: Smoke is the magician's prop, yet in reality it signals a fire coming, and no one plays when fire is on its way.

outline.heading: Pharaoh, the greatest deceiver
outline.gist: He deluded his people, claimed divinity and enslaved a whole race; wealth and strength gave him a false certainty that he need not take Musa seriously.

outline.heading: They left their gardens behind
outline.gist: The wealth that fed their false security passed to others when they perished.

outline.heading: Heaven and earth did not weep for them
outline.gist: We are not the centre of the universe; we matter only if Allah values us, and that ends arrogance.

outline.heading: Creation was not made in play
outline.gist: The cosmos was created with truth and purpose; do not make life about money, status or fame or use the deen for them.

outline.heading: The Day of Sorting and the tree of zaqqum
outline.gist: No one benefits another except by Allah's mercy; trees are something we take lightly, so see if you can take this one lightly.

outline.heading: The closing command: wait and watch
outline.gist: Those who took it lightly will see what comes; the evidence is already visible, so why keep playing.
